\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} SDET(R, m, n, A, s) is the set of determinants of SUBMATRIX(A, s, p, q) for INJECTIVE index maps p, q, where the notes use increasing ones; it is the notes' sdet\_sigma together with the negatives of its elements, so 'identical up to sign' under an F operation becomes equality of the two sets. Stated over a commutative ring; the H companions sdet-col-scale and sdet-row-scale are not in the notes.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.31}
\begin{cor}[{The gcd of the sigma-th subdeterminants is an invariant over Z}]\label{thm:sdet-gcd-invariant}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{sdet-gcd-invariant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, s, a, b, d, e. \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad s \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}is\text{-}gcd\text{-}set}(\operatorname{sdet}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a, s), d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}is\text{-}gcd\text{-}set}(\operatorname{sdet}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, b, s), e) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (d = e) \vee (d = -e) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{sdet-divisor-equiv}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, m, n, s, c, a, b.; \forall x \in \operatorname{sdet}(r, m, n, b, s). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \wedge \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad s \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{carr}(r) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(r)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(r, m, n, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{sdet}(r, m, n, a, s).\; \exists y \in \operatorname{carr}(r).\; (x = \operatorname{mul}(r)(c, y)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists y \in \operatorname{carr}(r).\; (x = \operatorname{mul}(r)(c, y)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{sdet-gcd-invariant}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/la-\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}gcd.scm} --- 117 recorded steps.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{zz-is-commutative-ring}, \texttt{zz-is-ring}, \texttt{elem-equiv-symmetric}, \texttt{lzg-zz-to-ring}, \texttt{sdet-divisor-equiv}, \texttt{lzg-ring-to-zz}, \texttt{zz-divides-antisym}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{sdet-divisor-equiv}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/la-\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}gcd.scm} --- 38 recorded steps.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{commutative-ring-is-ring}, \texttt{elem-gen-mat}, \texttt{matmul-type}, \texttt{sdet-divisor-row-gen}, \texttt{sdet-divisor-col-gen}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{crs}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} SDET uses injective index maps where the notes use increasing ones (see 3.29); no gcd changes. A -$>$ B is ELEM-EQUIV(ZZ-RING, m, n, A, B): B = P A Q with P, Q in ELEM-GEN. A gcd of a set is ZZ-IS-GCD-SET(S, d), and the conclusion is d = e or d = -e for any gcd d of SDET(A) and e of SDET(B). The notes' ideal argument is replaced by its divisor form.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.36}
\begin{prop}[{Integer normal form: existence and uniqueness of the diagonal form}]\label{thm:integer-normal-form}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{integer-normal-form}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, a. \\ \quad ((m \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z})))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists d \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(d, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(d, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(d, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall b \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(b, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(b, j, j)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad b = d \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{integer-normal-form-exists}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, a. \\ \quad ((m \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z})))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists d \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(d, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(d, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(d, j, j)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diagonal-normal-form-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, d, a. \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad d \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(d, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(a, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(d, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(d, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(a, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{elem\text{-}equiv}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d, a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad d = a \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diagonal-normal-form-unique-invertible}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, d, a, b, c. \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad d \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(d, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m).\; ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow (0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(a, i, i))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(d, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(d, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \operatorname{entry}(a, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, c) \wedge \\ \quad a = \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, b, d), c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad d = a \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diagonal-chain-sdet-gcd}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, d, s. \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad d \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i, j. \\ \quad \quad i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad i \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(d, i, i), \operatorname{entry}(d, j, j)) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad s \leq m \wedge \\ \quad s \leq n \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}is\text{-}gcd\text{-}set}(\operatorname{sdet}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, d, s), \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{prod\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, (\lambda k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, s).\; \operatorname{entry}(d, k, k)), \operatorname{interval}(1, s))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The relation \textasciitilde{} is ELEM-EQUIV(ZZ-RING, m, n, A, B): B = P A Q with P, Q in ELEM-GEN (over Z the row and the column elementary matrices form one set).  Existence (integer-normal-form-exists) gives a diagonal B with non-negative entries and the divisibility chain; uniqueness (diagonal-normal-form-unique, and diagonal-normal-form-unique-invertible for U D V with U, V invertible over Z) goes through diagonal-chain-sdet-gcd: b\_11 ... b\_ss is a gcd of the s-th subdeterminants.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.37}
\begin{cor}[{The reducing matrices U and V are products of elementary matrices}]\label{thm:integer-normal-form-elementary}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, a. \\ \quad ((m \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (a \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \mathbb{Z})))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists u \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m), v \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, m, n, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, u, a), v)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad 0 \leq \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, u, a), v), i, i) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ci}, j. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{ci} \leq j \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(\operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, u, a), v), \mathit{ci}, \mathit{ci}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, u, a), v), j, j)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/la-\allowbreak{}z3-\allowbreak{}smith.scm} --- 71 recorded steps.}

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.38}
\begin{cor}[{An invertible integer matrix is a product of elementary matrices}]\label{thm:zz-invertible-iff-elementary-product}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{zz-invertible-iff-elementary-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, u) \\ \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists p, q \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n). \\ \quad \quad u = \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, p, q) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{euclidean-invertible-iff-elem-gen}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(r) \wedge (n \in \mathbb{N})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(r, n, u) \Leftrightarrow (u \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(r, n)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{euclidean-unit-det-elem-gen}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(r) \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r)) \wedge \\ \quad \exists s \in \operatorname{carr}(r).\; (\operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, u), s) = \operatorname{one}(r)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(r, n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-gen-det-unit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, p. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (p \in \operatorname{elem\text{-}gen}(r, n)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists s \in \operatorname{carr}(r).\; (\operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, p), s) = \operatorname{one}(r)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.40}
\begin{lem}[{An invertible change of sequence preserves generation and freeness}]\label{thm:generates-transport}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{generates-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, u, m. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge ((u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d))) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge \operatorname{generates}(d, n, u)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, \operatorname{matact}(d, m, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, m, v, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge ((v \in \operatorname{mat}(m, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d))) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), m, a) \wedge \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, m, v)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, m, \operatorname{matact}(d, a, v)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{spans-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, u, m, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, u, a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, \operatorname{matact}(d, m, u), a) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.41}
\begin{prop}[{A relation-free sequence is no longer than a generating sequence}]\label{thm:free-length-le-generators}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-length-le-generators}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, m, u, v. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad v \in \operatorname{mat}(m, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, m, v) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad m \leq n \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-generating-length-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, m, u, v. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad m \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad v \in \operatorname{mat}(m, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, m, v) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, m, v) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad m = n \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.43}
\begin{cor}[{GL\_n(Z) acts freely and transitively on the free generating sequences}]\label{thm:free-generating-action-free}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-generating-action-free}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, m, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{matact}(d, m, s) = \operatorname{matact}(d, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad m = a \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-generating-action-stabilizer}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{matact}(d, m, s) = s \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad m = \operatorname{identmat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-generating-action-transitive}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists m.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge (a = \operatorname{matact}(d, m, s))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-generating-action-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, \operatorname{matact}(d, m, s)) \wedge \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, \operatorname{matact}(d, m, s)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.44}
\begin{prop}[{Adapted basis for a subgroup, with the divisibility chain}]\label{thm:principal-sequence-exists}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.45}
\begin{cor}[{The norm N\_F(E): the absolute determinant is basis-independent}]\label{thm:norm-independent}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{norm-independent}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, s_{2}, a, b, m, c, m_{2}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{scal}(d) = \operatorname{zz\text{-}ring} \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad s_{2} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, a, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, b, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, b) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad m_{2} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad a = \operatorname{matact}(d, c, s) \wedge \\ \quad b = \operatorname{matact}(d, m_{2}, s_{2}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \lvert \operatorname{det}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, m_{2}) \rvert = \lvert \operatorname{det}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, c) \rvert \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{change-of-basis-det-unit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, s, s_{2}, a, b, m, c, m_{2}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad s_{2} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, s_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, s_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, a, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, b, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, b) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(\operatorname{scal}(d))) \wedge \\ \quad m_{2} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(\operatorname{scal}(d))) \wedge \\ \quad a = \operatorname{matact}(d, c, s) \wedge \\ \quad b = \operatorname{matact}(d, m_{2}, s_{2}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists w \in \operatorname{carr}(\operatorname{scal}(d)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists v \in \operatorname{carr}(\operatorname{scal}(d)).\; (\operatorname{mul}(\operatorname{scal}(d))(w, v) = \operatorname{one}(\operatorname{scal}(d))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, m_{2}) = \operatorname{mul}(\operatorname{scal}(d))(w, \operatorname{det}(\operatorname{scal}(d), n, c)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.46}
\begin{cor}[{A subgroup of a free abelian group of rank n is free of rank at most n}]\label{thm:submodule-of-free-is-free}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d.; \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)), m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad (((k \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (k \leq n)) \wedge \exists w \in \operatorname{mat}(k, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)).\; (\operatorname{spans}(d, k, w, m) \wedge \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, k, w))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.47}
\begin{cor}[{A subgroup of an n-generated group is generated by at most n elements}]\label{thm:submodule-fg}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{submodule-fg}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d.; \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)), m. \\ \quad ((\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d))) \wedge (\operatorname{generates}(d, n, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, m))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((k \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (k \leq n)) \wedge \exists w \in \operatorname{mat}(k, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)).\; \operatorname{spans}(d, k, w, m) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{spans-submodule-fg}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d.; \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)), m, a \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{vec}(d)). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{spans}(d, n, u, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, a) \wedge \\ \quad a \subseteq m \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((k \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (k \leq n)) \wedge \exists w \in \operatorname{mat}(k, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)).\; \operatorname{spans}(d, k, w, a) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} This is the library's headline linear-algebra result, proven and billing modulo 0 since 2026-09-17.  Differences: it is stated for a MODULE over a euclidean ring (the notes' abelian group is not an instance, the abelian-group-as-ZZ-module view being absent), and its conclusion is a column family w in mat(k,1,vec(md)) with k $<$= n that SPANS the submodule.  spans-submodule-fg is the strictly more general form the descent actually needs: a submodule of a submodule spanned by n elements is spanned by k $<$= n.  The notes' own proof of this corollary (through Z\textasciicircum{}n and 3.44) is CIRCULAR -- Smith form consumes a finite generating set for F and cannot produce one -- so the library proves it directly, by descent on the ideal of last coefficients; the \textbackslash{}iffalse'd induction at tex:1651 is load-bearing in the notes.

\begin{lem}[{The quotient E/F for a diagonal subgroup}]\label{thm:quotient-by-diagonal-subgroup}
%

\vnbpart{\texttt{quotient-by-diagonal-subgroup}}

\vnbpart{\texttt{first-isomorphism-module}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, n, i, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}hom\text{-}module}(m, n, i) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(m, a) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{vec}(n).\; \exists x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; (i(x) = y) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; ((i(x) = \operatorname{vzero}(n)) \Leftrightarrow (x \in a)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{quotient\text{-}module}(m, a), n, \operatorname{descend}(\operatorname{qmod\text{-}setoid}(m, a), i)) \end{array}}

\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.50}
\begin{prop}[{Structure of a finitely generated abelian group}]\label{thm:fg-abelian-group-structure-exists}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{fg-abelian-group-structure-exists}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall e, n, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(e) \wedge ((\operatorname{scal}(e) = \operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(e))) \wedge \operatorname{generates}(e, n, u))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \mathbb{N}, a, f. \\ \quad \quad \quad (l \leq n) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(l, a) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(l, a), e, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fg-abelian-group-structure-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall e, l, a, f, c, b, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(e) \wedge \\ \quad l \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(l, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(c, b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(l, a), e, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(c, b), e, g) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (l = c) \wedge (a = b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cyclic-sum-iso-core}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, l, e, h. \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad l \in (\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad e \in (\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{Z}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; (0 \leq l(i)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; (0 \leq e(i)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i, j. \\ \quad \quad ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \wedge ((j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \wedge (i \leq j))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(l(i), l(j)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i, j. \\ \quad \quad ((i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \wedge ((j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \wedge (i \leq j))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{zz\text{-}divides}(e(i), e(j)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(n, l), \operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(n, e), h) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad l = e \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.51}
\begin{cor}[{Every finitely generated abelian group is a direct sum of cyclic groups}]\label{thm:fg-abelian-group-cyclic-decomposition}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{fg-abelian-group-cyclic-decomposition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall e, n, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(e) \wedge ((\operatorname{scal}(e) = \operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}) \wedge ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(e))) \wedge \operatorname{generates}(e, n, u))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \mathbb{N}, a. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(l, a) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists f.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(l, a), e, f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall c, b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((c \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(c, b) \wedge \exists g.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(c, b), e, g))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (l = c) \wedge (a = b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cyclic-sum-iso-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall l, a, c, b, h. \\ \quad l \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(l, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invariant\text{-}factors}(c, b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}iso\text{-}module}(\operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(l, a), \operatorname{cyclic\text{-}sum}(c, b), h) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (l = c) \wedge (a = b) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{fg-abelian-group-cyclic-decomposition}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/la-\allowbreak{}z4-\allowbreak{}unique.scm} --- 36 recorded steps.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{fg-abelian-group-structure-exists}, \texttt{fg-abelian-group-structure-unique}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{crs}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%

%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.52}
\begin{cor}[{The cardinality of E/F is the norm N\_E(F)}]\label{thm:quotient-card-norm}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{quotient-card-norm}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, n, u, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{scal}(d) = \operatorname{zz\text{-}ring} \wedge \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(d)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{generates}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, m) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{submodule\text{-}norm}(d, m) = 0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{vec}(\operatorname{quotient\text{-}module}(d, m))| = \operatorname{submodule\text{-}norm}(d, m) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cyclic-dsum-card}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, m. \\ \quad ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((m \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \mathbb{Z})) \wedge \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; (1 \leq \operatorname{entry}(m, i, i)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{vec}(\operatorname{direct\text{-}sum}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, (\lambda \mathit{fmi} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; \operatorname{zz\text{-}mod}(\operatorname{entry}(m, \mathit{fmi}, \mathit{fmi}))))) \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{vec}(\operatorname{direct\text{-}sum}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, (\lambda \mathit{fmi} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; \operatorname{zz\text{-}mod}(\operatorname{entry}(m, \mathit{fmi}, \mathit{fmi})))))| \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{vec}(\operatorname{direct\text{-}sum}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, n, (\lambda \mathit{fmi} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; \operatorname{zz\text{-}mod}(\operatorname{entry}(m, \mathit{fmi}, \mathit{fmi})))))| \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{prod\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, (\lambda k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; \operatorname{entry}(m, k, k)), \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{principal-sequence-of-presentation}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, m, n, u, s, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}module}(d) \wedge ((\operatorname{scal}(d) = \operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(d, m) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}norm\text{-}data}(d, m, n, u, s, a)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists b, c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}principal\text{-}sequence}(d, n, m, b, c) \wedge \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(d, n, \operatorname{matact}(d, c, b)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{dsum-card}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, f. \\ \quad n \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; (\operatorname{vec}(f(i)) \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; (|\operatorname{vec}(f(i))| \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{dsum\text{-}vec}(n, f)| \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{dsum\text{-}vec}(n, f)| \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{prod\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}ring}, (\lambda k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; |\operatorname{vec}(f(k))|), \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{zz-mod-card}}
\vnbstmt{\forall b \in \mathbb{Z}.\; ((1 \leq b) \Rightarrow (|\operatorname{vec}(\operatorname{zz\text{-}mod}(b))| = b))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{card-cartesian}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbf{Set}. \\ \quad ((|a| \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (|b| \in \mathbb{N})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad |(a \times b)| = (|a| \cdot |b|) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{quotient-card-norm}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/la-\allowbreak{}z5-\allowbreak{}card52.scm} --- 250 recorded steps.}

\section{Complex analysis}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.2}
\begin{prop}[{Uniqueness of the least upper bound}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.2}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{rr\text{-}upper\text{-}bound}(s, a) \wedge \\ \quad \forall c.\; (\operatorname{rr\text{-}upper\text{-}bound}(s, c) \Rightarrow (a \leq c)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{rr\text{-}upper\text{-}bound}(s, b) \wedge \\ \quad \forall c.\; (\operatorname{rr\text{-}upper\text{-}bound}(s, c) \Rightarrow (b \leq c)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad a = b \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/rabasics-\allowbreak{}order.scm} --- 37 recorded steps.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{rr-leq-antisymmetric}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} none.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} A least upper bound is an RR-UPPER-BOUND that is $<$= every upper bound (Definition 1.8); no guard on the set. (calculus 1.9 and complex-analysis 1.2 share this statement.)
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.3}
\begin{prop}[{C as 2x2 real matrices}]\label{thm:cc-matrix-representation}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-matrix-representation}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep} \in \mathrm{Bij}(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrices}) \wedge \\ \forall z, w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}((z + w)) \\ \quad =\; \operatorname{matadd}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(z), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(w)) \wedge \\ \forall z, w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}((z \cdot w)) \\ \quad =\; \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(z), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(w)) \wedge \\ \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(1) = \operatorname{identmat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2) \wedge \\ \forall c \in \mathbb{R}, z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}((c \cdot z)) \\ \quad =\; \operatorname{matscale}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), c, \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep}(z)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-matrix-rep-bijection}}
\vnbstmt{\operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}rep} \in \mathrm{Bij}(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrices})}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-matrix-of-mul}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}of}(a, b), \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}of}(c, d)) \\ \quad =\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}matrix\text{-}of}(((a \cdot c) - (b \cdot d)), ((a \cdot d) + (b \cdot c))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.5}
\begin{prop}[{Unions and finite intersections of open sets}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.5}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{union-of-opens-open}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, g. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \forall i \in a.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, g(i))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(i, a, g(i))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{inter-of-finite-opens-open}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s.; \forall c \in \mathbf{Set}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge ((|c| \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (\exists w.\; (w \in c) \wedge \forall u \in c.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, u)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, \operatorname{intersection\text{-}of}(c)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

%

%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.7}
\begin{prop}[{Monotone convergence for real sequences}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.7}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{monotone-converges-to-sup}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad (\forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \leq f((k + 1))) \wedge \exists d \in \mathbb{R}.\; \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \leq d)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, \operatorname{sup}(\{y \in \mathbb{R} : \exists a \in \mathbb{N}.\; (y = f(a))\})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{monotone-converges-to-inf-literal}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad (\forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f((k + 1)) \leq f(k)) \wedge \exists d \in \mathbb{R}.\; \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (d \leq f(k))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, \operatorname{inf}(\{y \in \mathbb{R} : \exists a \in \mathbb{N}.\; (y = f(a))\})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{monotone-converges-to-sup}}}
%

%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.9}
\begin{prop}[{Closed sets and limits of sequences}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.9}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-iff-sequentially-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (a \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a) \Leftrightarrow \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to a), l.\; (\operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l) \Rightarrow (l \in a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{seq-closed-implies-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \\ \quad a \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to a), l.\; (\operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l) \Rightarrow (l \in a)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-limit-in}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a.; \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to a), l. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a) \wedge \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l))) \Rightarrow (l \in a) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{pts}(s)).\; \exists x.\; \operatorname{cluster\text{-}point}(s, f, x) \end{array}}

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow (\operatorname{totally\text{-}bounded}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(s)) \end{array}}

\end{prop}

(3) is stated with CLUSTER-POINT defined by: for every eps $>$ 0 and every m in NN there is n $>$= m with dist(f(n), x) $<$ eps -- the notes define a cluster point by the set \{n : x\_n in B(y,r)\} being infinite.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.12}
\begin{prop}[{Product of numbers in polar form}]\label{thm:cc-cos-add}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-cos-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall z, w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \cos (z + w) = ((\cos z \cdot \cos w) - (\sin z \cdot \sin w)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-sin-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall z, w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \sin (z + w) = ((\cos w \cdot \sin z) + (\cos z \cdot \sin w)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-add}}
\vnbstmt{\forall z, w \in \mathbb{C}.\; (\exp (z + w) = (\exp z \cdot \exp w))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-polar-form}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg (w = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists r, h \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < r) \wedge ((-\pi \leq h) \wedge ((h < \pi) \wedge (w = (r \cdot \exp (+i \cdot h))))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.14}
\begin{lem}[{Positive orientation of a triangular path by angles}]\label{thm:positively-oriented-iff}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c. \\ \quad a \in \mathbb{C} \wedge \\ \quad b \in \mathbb{C} \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{C} \wedge \\ \quad \neg (a = b) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (b = c) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (c = a) \wedge \\ \quad \exists v.\; (v \in \operatorname{interior}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{conv3}(a, b, c))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{positively\text{-}oriented}(a, b, c) \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists u \in \operatorname{interior}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{conv3}(a, b, c)). \\ \quad \quad \quad ((\operatorname{angle}((b - u), (a - u)) < \pi) \wedge ((\operatorname{angle}((c - u), (b - u)) < \pi) \wedge (\operatorname{angle}((a - u), (c - u)) < \pi))) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/triangle-\allowbreak{}orientation.scm} --- 191 recorded steps.}
%

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{sos}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.15}
\begin{thm}[{C is an algebraically closed field}]\label{thm:cc-algebraically-closed}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-algebraically-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad ((1 \leq n) \wedge \neg (p(n) = 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k))), (n + 1)) = 0 \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fundamental-theorem-of-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), m \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \neg (p((m + 1)) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k))), ((m + 1) + 1)) = 0 \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-polynomial-lower-growth}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), m \in \mathbb{N}, z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad 1 \leq \operatorname{magnitude}(z) \wedge \\ \quad 2 \cdot \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{magnitude}(p(k))), (m + 1)) \\ \quad \leq\; \operatorname{magnitude}(p((m + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(z) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{magnitude}(p((m + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{magnitude}(z), (m + 1)) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; 2 \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k))), ((m + 1) + 1))) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/ca1-\allowbreak{}alg-\allowbreak{}closed.scm} --- 16 recorded steps.}

\begin{lem}[{Convergence in the extended plane}]\label{thm:cc-hat-converges-iff}

\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-hat-converges-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), x \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \operatorname{top\text{-}converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}hat\text{-}top}, f, x) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, f, x) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-hat-converges-inf-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \operatorname{top\text{-}converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}hat\text{-}top}, f, \operatorname{cc\text{-}inf}) \\ \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \forall m \in \mathbb{R}. \exists n \in \mathbb{N}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (n \leq k) \Rightarrow (m \leq \operatorname{magnitude}(f(k))) \end{array}}

\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.18}
\begin{prop}[{Linear maps on C\textasciicircum{}2 and linear fractional transformations}]\label{thm:mat-lft-in-lfts}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{mat-lft-in-lfts}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(s) \in \mathit{lfts} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mat-lft-hom}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, t) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(\operatorname{matmul}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), s, t)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{compose}(\operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(s), \operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(t)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mat-lft-onto}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in \mathit{lfts}. \exists s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, s) \wedge (f = \operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(s))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mat-lft-kernel}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(s) = \operatorname{id\text{-}fun}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}hat})) \Leftrightarrow \exists r \in \mathbb{C}.\; (s = [[r, 0], [0, r]]) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{lft-homog}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, d, u, v \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (\neg (((a \cdot d) - (b \cdot c)) = 0) \wedge \neg ((u = 0) \wedge (v = 0))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{lft}(a, b, c, d)(\operatorname{homog\text{-}point}(u, v)) = \operatorname{homog\text{-}point}(((a \cdot u) + (b \cdot v)), ((c \cdot u) + (d \cdot v))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{lft-compose}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, d, f, g, h, k \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (\neg (((a \cdot d) - (b \cdot c)) = 0) \wedge \neg (((f \cdot k) - (g \cdot h)) = 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{compose}(\operatorname{lft}(a, b, c, d), \operatorname{lft}(f, g, h, k)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{lft}(((a \cdot f) + (b \cdot h)), ((a \cdot g) + (b \cdot k)), ((c \cdot f) + (d \cdot h)), ((c \cdot g) + (d \cdot k))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s \in \operatorname{mat}(2, 2, \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{det}(\operatorname{normed\text{-}field\text{-}as\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}), 2, s) = 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{mat\text{-}lft}(s) = \operatorname{id\text{-}fun}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}hat})) \Leftrightarrow ((s = [[1, 0], [0, 1]]) \vee (s = [[-1, 0], [0, -1]])) \end{array}}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.22}
\begin{prop}[{The Hopf map is continuous and onto S\textasciicircum{}2}]\label{thm:hopf-maps-sphere}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-maps-sphere}}
\vnbstmt{\forall w \in \operatorname{cc2\text{-}sphere}.\; (\operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(w) \in \operatorname{unit\text{-}sphere\text{-}cr})}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-onto-sphere}}
\vnbstmt{\forall p \in \operatorname{unit\text{-}sphere\text{-}cr}.\; \exists w \in \operatorname{cc2\text{-}sphere}.\; (\operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(w) = p)}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-map-continuous-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(\operatorname{product2\text{-}ms}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}), \operatorname{product2\text{-}ms}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}), \\ \quad (\lambda v \in (\mathbb{C} \times \mathbb{C}).\; \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(v))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-map-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, b, x. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, \operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, a, x) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, \operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, b, x)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, \operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, (\lambda z \in \operatorname{pts}(s).\; \operatorname{nth}(1, \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}([a(z), b(z)]))), x) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, (\lambda z \in \operatorname{pts}(s).\; \operatorname{nth}(2, \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}([a(z), b(z)]))), x) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-norm-identity}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{magnitude}((2 \cdot (a \cdot \operatorname{conjugate}(b)))) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}((2 \cdot (a \cdot \operatorname{conjugate}(b))))) + (((\operatorname{magnitude}(a) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(a)) - (\operatorname{magnitude}(b) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(b))) \cdot ((\operatorname{magnitude}(a) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(a)) - (\operatorname{magnitude}(b) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(b)))) \\ \quad =\; ((\operatorname{magnitude}(a) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(a)) + (\operatorname{magnitude}(b) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(b))) \cdot ((\operatorname{magnitude}(a) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(a)) + (\operatorname{magnitude}(b) \cdot \operatorname{magnitude}(b))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

Continuity is IS-CONTINUOUS(C\textasciicircum{}2, C x R, pi) (hopf-map-continuous-product), assembled from the general form hopf-map-continuous (for u1, u2 : S -$>$ C continuous at x, the two coordinates of z |-$>$ pi(u1(z), u2(z)) are continuous at x) and the pairing property of the product. \renewcommand{\thethm}{1.24}
\begin{cor}[{The Hopf fibration factors through a bijection S\textasciicircum{}2 -$>$ P}]\label{thm:hopf-factors-through-bijection}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-factors-through-bijection}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \exists g \in (\operatorname{unit\text{-}sphere\text{-}cr} \to \operatorname{cc\text{-}hat}). \\ \quad g \in \mathrm{Bij}(\operatorname{unit\text{-}sphere\text{-}cr}, \operatorname{cc\text{-}hat}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall u \in \operatorname{cc2\text{-}sphere}.\; (g(\operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(u)) = \operatorname{homog\text{-}point}(\operatorname{nth}(1, u), \operatorname{nth}(2, u))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-fibre-equiv}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, v \in \operatorname{cc2\text{-}sphere}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(u) = \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(v)) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{homog\text{-}equiv}(u, v) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hopf-fibre-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, v \in \operatorname{cc2\text{-}sphere}. \\ \quad \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(u) = \operatorname{hopf\text{-}map}(v) \\ \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists r \in \mathbb{C}.\; ((\operatorname{magnitude}(r) = 1) \wedge (v = [(r \cdot \operatorname{nth}(1, u)), (r \cdot \operatorname{nth}(2, u))])) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k, u, f, a, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, f, a, l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(\operatorname{nf\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(k), u), \operatorname{nf\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(k), f, a) \end{array}}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3}
\begin{prop}[{Sum and product rules}]\label{thm:diff-on-sum}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k, u, f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, f, a, l) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, g, a, m))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, (\lambda x \in u.\; \operatorname{add}(k)(f(x), g(x))), a, \operatorname{add}(k)(l, m)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k, u, f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, f, a, l) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, g, a, m))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, (\lambda x \in u.\; \operatorname{mul}(k)(f(x), g(x))), a, \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{add}(k)(\operatorname{mul}(k)(l, g(a)), \operatorname{mul}(k)(m, f(a)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{holomorphic-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, f, g, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, g) \wedge \\ \quad m \in (u \to \mathbb{C}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in u.\; (m(x) \simeq (f(x) + g(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, m) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{holomorphic-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, f, g, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, g) \wedge \\ \quad m \in (u \to \mathbb{C}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in u.\; (m(x) \simeq (f(x) \cdot g(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, m) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Two separate developments, neither of which is exactly the notes' statement. diff-on-sum / diff-on-product give the derivative at a, but only for the LITERAL function VNB-LAMBDA x in U. (add K)(f(x), g(x)) (resp. the product); a pointwise-equal representative of f + g or f . g has to be transported by diff-on-transfer-ptwise-eq. holomorphic-sum / holomorphic-product do take an arbitrary sm in FUN(U, CC) that agrees pointwise, but they conclude only HOLOMORPHIC-ON(U, sm) and say nothing about the value of the derivative at a. Both diff-on laws are stated for a general normed field K.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3.3.1}
\begin{defn}[{The principal branch of the logarithm}]\label{thm:cc-log-spec}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-spec}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(w) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left(w\right) \in \mathbb{C} \wedge \\ \quad \quad -\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right)) < \pi \wedge \\ \quad \quad \exp \log\left(w\right) = w \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-log}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(w) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow (\exp \log\left(w\right) = w) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-exp}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad ((-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(z)) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(z) < \pi)) \Rightarrow (\log\left(\exp z\right) = z) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-char}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w, z \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad ((-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(z)) \wedge ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(z) < \pi) \wedge (\exp z = w))) \Rightarrow (\log\left(w\right) = z) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad -\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(a) < \pi \wedge \\ \quad -\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(b) < \pi \wedge \\ \quad \exp a = \exp b \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad a = b \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-real}}
\vnbstmt{\forall t \in \mathbb{R}.\; ((0 < t) \Rightarrow (\log\left(t\right) = \log\left(t\right)))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-one}}
\vnbstmt{\log\left(1\right) = 0}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-polar}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, h \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < r) \wedge ((-\pi < h) \wedge (h < \pi))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left((r \cdot \exp (+i \cdot h))\right) = (\log\left(r\right) + (+i \cdot h)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s \in \mathbb{R}, w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad ((0 < s) \wedge \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(w) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w) \leq 0))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left((s \cdot w)\right) = (\log\left(s\right) + \log\left(w\right)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-in-slit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(w) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(w\right) \in \mathbb{C}) \wedge ((-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right))) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right)) < \pi)) \end{array}}
%
\end{defn}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} DEFINED 2026-09-27 (batch 38): CC-LOG(w) is the IOTA of the z with -pi $<$ Im z $<$ pi and exp z = w, for w in the slit plane \{u in cc : not(Im u = 0 and Re u $<$= 0)\} (structure-library/analytic-log.scm); existence is cc-exp-open-strip-onto (batch 34), uniqueness cc-log-unique, the characterisation cc-log-spec by iota-d. Laws: exp(log w) = w, log(exp z) = z on the strip, log = LOG on the positive reals (through the bridge cc-exp-real-is-r-exp), log 1 = 0, the polar form (40) log(r exp(i th)) = LOG r + i th, log(s w) = LOG s + log w for real s $>$ 0.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3.3.1-hol}
\begin{prop}[{log is holomorphic on C minus (-inf, 0]}]\label{thm:cc-log-holomorphic}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\{u \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0))\}, \\ \quad (\lambda w \in \{u \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0))\}.\; \log\left(w\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-deriv}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall b \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(b) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(b) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \{u \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0))\}, \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda w \in \{u \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0))\}.\; \log\left(w\right)), \\ \quad \quad \quad b, \operatorname{recip}(b)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-at}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(a) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(a) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists p \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad 0 < p \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, a, p) \subseteq \{u \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0))\} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, a, p), (\lambda x \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, a, p).\; \log\left(x\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-im-near-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall d, r \in \mathbb{R}, z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, r). \\ \quad ((0 < d) \wedge ((0 < r) \wedge (((r \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \wedge ((r \cdot (1 + d)) \leq d)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(z) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(z) \leq 0)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad -d < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(z\right)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(z\right)) < d \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-rotate}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w)) \Rightarrow (\log\left((+i \cdot w)\right) = (\log\left(w\right) + (+i \cdot (1/2 \cdot \pi)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-rotate-neg}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w)) \Rightarrow (\log\left((-+i \cdot w)\right) = (\log\left(w\right) - (+i \cdot (1/2 \cdot \pi)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-mul}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, v \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(u) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(u) \leq 0)) \wedge \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(v) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(v) \leq 0)) \wedge \\ \quad -\pi < (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(u\right)) + \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(v\right))) \wedge \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(u\right)) + \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(v\right))) < \pi \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \log\left((u \cdot v)\right) = (\log\left(u\right) + \log\left(v\right)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-right-half}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall w \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(w)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (-(1/2 \cdot \pi) < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right))) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(w\right)) < (1/2 \cdot \pi)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-pi-gt-three}}
\vnbstmt{3 < \pi}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-cos-pos-half}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((-(1/2 \cdot \pi) < t) \wedge (t < (1/2 \cdot \pi))) \Rightarrow (0 < \cos t) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-near-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < r) \wedge ((r \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, r), (\lambda z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, r).\; \log\left(z\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, s \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < r) \wedge (((r \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \wedge (0 < s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, s, (s \cdot r)), (\lambda z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, s, (s \cdot r)).\; \log\left(z\right))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-27 (batch 38-B), with the derivative log'(w) = recip(w) (cc-log-deriv). THE ROUTE DIFFERS FROM THE NOTES: no sector cover and no numerical bound on pi is needed -- at every point a of the slit plane, log x = log a + log(x / a) on the ball B(a, |a| r) with r = (pi - |Im log a|) / (2 (1 + pi)), where log(x / a) is the power series near 1 (cc-log-holomorphic-at, cc-log-im-near-one). The notes' rotation laws log(i w) = log w + i pi/2 (cc-log-rotate, from cos $>$ 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2), cc-cos-pos-half) and pi $>$ 3 (cc-pi-gt-three, from cos(3/2) $>$ 0 by six terms of the series) are proven as well. Earlier: PARTIAL 2026-09-27 (batch 38): holomorphic on B(1, pi/(1+pi)) (as the power series log0) and on every scaled ball B(s, s pi/(1+pi)), s $>$ 0, by log(s w) = LOG s + log w. The rotation step log(i w) = log w + i pi/2 and the cover of the slit plane need cos $>$ 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2) and pi $>$ 3, which the tree lacked: batch 38-B.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.4}
\begin{prop}[{Chain Rule}]\label{thm:diff-on-chain}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k, u, s, f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, f, a, l) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, s, g, f(a), m) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in u.\; (f(y) \in s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, (\lambda x \in u.\; g(f(x))), a, \operatorname{mul}(k)(m, l)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

The composite is the literal VNB-LAMBDA x in U. g(f(x)), so a pointwise-equal representative needs diff-on-transfer-ptwise-eq; the derivative is written (mul K)(m, l) in the normed field K. Stated for a general K, not specialised to CC.

\end{lem}

\begin{prop}[{Radius of convergence by the root test}]\label{thm:cps-radius-root}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda j \in \mathbb{N}.\; {\operatorname{magnitude}(f(j))}^{{j}^{\ast\!-1}})) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf} \wedge \\ \quad (\operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda j \in \mathbb{N}.\; {\operatorname{magnitude}(f(j))}^{{j}^{\ast\!-1}})) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda j \in \mathbb{N}.\; {\operatorname{magnitude}(f(j))}^{{j}^{\ast\!-1}})) \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < \operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda j \in \mathbb{N}.\; {\operatorname{magnitude}(f(j))}^{{j}^{\ast\!-1}})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) = \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda j \in \mathbb{N}.\; {\operatorname{magnitude}(f(j))}^{{j}^{\ast\!-1}}))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.9}
\begin{lem}[{Polynomially bounded factors do not shrink the radius}]\label{thm:cps-radius-factor}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, a \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), c \in \mathbb{R}, m \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad (\forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (a(k) = (f(k) \cdot g(k))) \wedge \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{magnitude}(g(k)) \leq (c \cdot \operatorname{power}(k, m)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) \leq \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(a) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/cc-\allowbreak{}power-\allowbreak{}series-\allowbreak{}laws.scm} --- 130 recorded steps.}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.10}
\begin{prop}[{A power series is holomorphic and differentiates termwise}]\label{thm:cps-holomorphic-ball}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-holomorphic-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), r \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < r) \wedge (r < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k)))))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; ((n + 1) \cdot f((n + 1))))) = \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall a \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad a, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (((k + 1) \cdot f((k + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{power}(a, k))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-radius-derived}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall j \in \mathbb{N}.\; (a(j) = ((j + 1) \cdot f((j + 1)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(a) = \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-diff-on-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), r \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{cpda} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r). \\ \quad (\forall j \in \mathbb{N}.\; (a(j) = ((j + 1) \cdot f((j + 1)))) \wedge ((0 < r) \wedge (r < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(f)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda z \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, r).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(z, k))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \mathit{cpda}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (a(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpda}, k))))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-24 (batch 26-A, theorem-library/cc-power-series-deriv.scm): PROVEN with one convention -- the library has no ball of radius +inf, so the statement is made on B(0, r) for every real 0 $<$ r $<$ R (which covers B(0, R) for finite R and CC for R = +inf): f is holomorphic on B(0, r), the derived series sum (k+1) a\_(k+1) z\textasciicircum{}k has the same radius, and f'(u) is its sum. The proof avoids the notes' double sum and lim n\textasciicircum{}(1/n) = 1 (absent): a one-step recurrence gives the second-order estimate, a radius-comparison lemma and Lemma 2.9 with b\_k = k give the radius. EARLIER NOTE: Nothing near, in either the complex or the real case. The library's power series are real and pointwise (PS-CONVERGES-AT); it has no theorem that the sum function of a power series is differentiable, no termwise-differentiated series, and no statement that the two series share a radius. HOLOMORPHIC-ON is available (holomorphic-basics.scm) but the only holomorphic functions exhibited are constants, the identity, powers, sums and products (holomorphic-const, holomorphic-identity, holomorphic-power, holomorphic-sum, holomorphic-product).
