\begin{prop}[{A subterm of an encryption under one key that is an encryption under another lies inside the plaintext}]\label{thm:subterm-encr-other-key}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, h, a, y, b. \\ \quad t \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k) \wedge \\ \quad y \in k \wedge \\ \quad b \in k \wedge \\ \quad \neg (y = b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(t, k, \operatorname{encr}(a, b), \operatorname{encr}(h, y)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(t, k, \operatorname{encr}(a, b), h) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.3}
\begin{prop}[{The adversary bound: a secret that never originates on a regular node occurs nowhere}]\label{thm:adversary-bound}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{adversary-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, u.; \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (u \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \Rightarrow \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), u, n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), u, \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{adversary-bound-adversary-nodes}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, u.; \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (u \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \Rightarrow \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), u, n) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), u, \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{adversary-node-origin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, u, n. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad n \in \operatorname{nodes}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, n) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), u, n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p) \end{array}}

The adversary has the traces M F T C S E D over the space (C and S n-ary over lists; D decrypts under KINV; the paper's K trace is subsumed by M since keys are tokens). The proof is the paper's method -- a minimal member of \{n in C : u @ content(n)\} by Lemma 2.7, originating by 2.9, sent by 2.8, hence an adversary node, then seven cases -- with two findings: the M and C cases rest on the TOKEN LAW (no token is a list), not on the freeness of a free algebra; and the E case holds under either subterm convention, the convention deciding only whether the hypothesis 'never originates regularly' can be met for a key a participant encrypts with. \renewcommand{\thethm}{5.3}
\begin{lem}[{The responder's nonce originates at the responder's second node}]\label{thm:nsl-resp-nonce-originates}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, c, d. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}pk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}resp\text{-}strand}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (c = d) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), d, [2, s]) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\begin{lem}[{The strand through n1 and n2 is an initiator strand in C}]\label{thm:nsl-lemma-5-7}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, a, b, c, d, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}nsl\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{nodes}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p), b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sent}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), a) = \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([f, g, d]), \operatorname{pubkey}(p)(c)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}init\text{-}strand}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{nth}(2, b)), c, d, f, g) \wedge (\operatorname{nth}(1, b) = 3)) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.8}
\begin{prop}[{Injectivity: at most one initiator strand for a uniquely originating Na}]\label{thm:nsl-init-unique}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{nsl-init-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, a, b, c, d, f, g, a_{2}, b_{2}, h. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}pk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), f) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}init\text{-}strand}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(a), c, d, f, g) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}init\text{-}strand}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(b), a_{2}, b_{2}, f, h) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad a = b \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{nsl-init-nonce-originates}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, t, a, b, c, d. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}pk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad t \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}init\text{-}strand}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(t), a, b, c, d) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), c, [1, t]) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The original protocol is the vocabulary structure-library/nso.scm: IS-NSO-INIT-STRAND, IS-NSO-RESP-STRAND, IS-NSO-SPACE, the NSL definitions with the second message \{Na Nb\}\_KA. Hypotheses those of Proposition 5.2 (K\_A\textasciicircum{}-1 uncompromised, Na /= Nb, Nb uniquely originating). The proof is the NSL proof of Lemmas 5.3, 5.4, 5.6 run unchanged on the new vocabulary (theorem-library/nso-laws.scm, a token-aware copy of nsl.scm sections 1-11): nothing up to Lemma 5.6 reads B off v0, which is the paper's 'exactly parallel'. The NS analogue of Lemma 5.7 fails (Lowe's attack); no attack bundle is constructed. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-1).

(\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{pubkey}(p)(a)) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{pubkey}(p)(b)) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (d = f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), f, \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), g)) \wedge \\ \quad \neg \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([d, f, b]), \operatorname{pubkey}(p)(a)), \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), g)) \wedge \\ \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{encr}(f, \operatorname{pubkey}(p)(b)), \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), g)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), f, \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), z)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([d, f, b]), \operatorname{pubkey}(p)(a)), \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), z)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{encr}(f, \operatorname{pubkey}(p)(b)), \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{pk\text{-}inf}(p)), z)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg ([z, g] \in \renewcommand{\thethm}{6.3}
\begin{prop}[{The ideal generated by a set is the union of the principal ideals}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-union}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-union}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s. \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge (\forall y \in a.\; (y \in k) \wedge \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) = \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(x, s, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, \operatorname{singleton}(x))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-is-ideal}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s. \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge \forall y \in a.\; (y \in k))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}key\text{-}ideal}(t, k, a, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-least}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, i.; \forall m \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s). \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}key\text{-}ideal}(t, k, a, i) \wedge \forall z \in s.\; (z \in i)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad m \in i \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} On the user's model (tokens, n-ary LST, ENCR): a KS-ideal (IS-KEY-IDEAL, structure-library/strand-ideals.scm) is a subset I of A = MSG-SET(T, K) holding LST(l) whenever some component of the list l is in I (the n-ary join) and ENCR(h, y) for h in I, y in KS; I\_k[S] is KEY-IDEAL-GEN(T, K, KS, S), the intersection of the KS-ideals in POWER(A) containing S; I\_k[x] is KEY-IDEAL-GEN(T, K, KS, SINGLETON(x)). The paper's k and K are one folded symbol: the key subset is KS. Hypotheses as the paper's (S a subset of A, KS a subset of K) plus T and K sets. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-1).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{6.4}
\begin{lem}[{The generated ideal by stages of encryption}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-stages}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-stages}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s. \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge (\forall y \in a.\; (y \in k) \wedge \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(i, \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, \emptyset, \operatorname{ideal\text{-}stage}(t, k, a, s, i))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ideal-stage-in-gen}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall i \in \mathbb{N}, t, k, a, s.; \forall z \in \operatorname{ideal\text{-}stage}(t, k, a, s, i). \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge (\forall y \in a.\; (y \in k) \wedge \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad z \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ideal-stage-in-power}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall i \in \mathbb{N}, t, k, a, s. \\ \quad ((t \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{ideal\text{-}stage}(t, k, a, s, i) \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \end{array}}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The stages are IDEAL-STAGE(T, K, KS, S, i), a def-by-nn-recursion: S\_0 = S, S\_(i+1) = \{ENCR(g, y) : g in I\_empty[S\_i], y in KS\}; I\_empty[-] is KEY-IDEAL-GEN with the key set EMPTY-SET. The paper's 'by induction, S\_i is a subset of I\_k[S]' is ideal-stage-in-gen (an induction on i using that a KS-ideal is an empty-set-ideal, key-ideal-empty-keys). Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-1).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{6.6}
\begin{prop}[{Decryption stays in the ideal of simple terms}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-decrypt}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-decrypt}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, h, y. \\ \quad t \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall w \in a.\; (w \in k) \wedge \\ \quad y \in k \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall u \in s.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}msg}(t, k, u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall u \in s, g.\; \neg (u = \operatorname{encr}(g, y)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{encr}(h, y) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad h \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-cases}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, x. \\ \quad t \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad x \in s \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)). \\ \quad \quad \quad x = \operatorname{lst}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists j \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (1 \leq j) \wedge ((j \leq \operatorname{length}(l)) \wedge (\operatorname{nth}(j, l) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s), y \in a.\; (x = \operatorname{encr}(h, y)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

The paper's 'I' = I\_k[S] minus \{h\}\_K' argument is done once for 6.6, 6.7 and 6.8 as the inversion lemma key-ideal-gen-cases (a member of I\_k[S] is in S, or a list message with a component in I\_k[S], or an encryption of a member of I\_k[S] under a key of KS); 6.6 is one case analysis of it. Stated as the notes state it; the hypotheses 'every s in S is simple' and 'K a key' are not used by the proof. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-1).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{6.7}
\begin{prop}[{Only keys of k encrypt into the ideal of simple terms}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-encr-key}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-encr-key}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, h, y. \\ \quad t \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall w \in a.\; (w \in k) \wedge \\ \quad y \in k \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall u \in s.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}msg}(t, k, u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall u \in s, g.\; \neg (u = \operatorname{encr}(g, y)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{encr}(h, y) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad y \in a \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-cases}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, x. \\ \quad t \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad x \in s \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)). \\ \quad \quad \quad x = \operatorname{lst}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists j \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (1 \leq j) \wedge ((j \leq \operatorname{length}(l)) \wedge (\operatorname{nth}(j, l) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s), y \in a.\; (x = \operatorname{encr}(h, y)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{6.9}
\begin{prop}[{A minimal node with term in I is an entry point for I}]\label{thm:bundle-minimal-entry-point}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{bundle-minimal-entry-point}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, i, n. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), n) \in i \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), z) \in i) \Rightarrow \neg ([z, n] \in \operatorname{precedes\text{-}strict}(c)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}entry\text{-}point}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), n, i) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bundle-minimal-sent}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, s, n. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x, y. \\ \quad \quad x \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad y \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), x) = \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), y) \wedge \\ \quad \quad y \in s \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad x \in s \wedge \\ \quad n \in s \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; \neg ([z, n] \in \operatorname{precedes\text{-}strict}(c)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sent}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bundle-ssb-precedes}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, x, y. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge ((y \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c)) \wedge \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), x, y))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad [x, y] \in \operatorname{precedes\text{-}strict}(c) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bundle-ssb-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c.; \forall y \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c), x. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{bspace}(c), x, y)) \Rightarrow (x \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Stated for any class I of messages: n in BNODES(c), NODE-CONTENT(n) in I, and no z in BNODES(c) with content in I strictly precedes n, give IS-ENTRY-POINT(BSPACE(c), n, I). The two steps of the paper are bundle-minimal-sent (the set is closed under equal content, so its minimal member is SENT) and bundle-ssb-closed / bundle-ssb-precedes (an earlier node on the same strand is in the bundle and precedes); 'n' =$>$+ n' is the strict same-strand order (D4). bundle-minimal-originates is the instance I = \{m : u subterm of m\}. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-1).

\begin{thm}[{Ideals generated by atoms are honest}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-honest}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-honest}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, a, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)).\; ((y \in s) \vee (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(y) \in a)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}honest}(p, c, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{adversary-sent-shapes}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad m \in \operatorname{nodes}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sent}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}text\text{-}trace}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p), \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(\operatorname{nth}(2, m))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{lst}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((1 \leq i) \wedge (i \leq \operatorname{length}(l))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{nth}(i, l)) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)))), q \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad 1 \leq q \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad q \leq \operatorname{length}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{nth}(q, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{lst}(l)) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))), k \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{encr}(h, k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = h) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))), k \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = h \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(k))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{encr}(h, k)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-decrypt-atoms}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, h, y. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}token\text{-}set}(t) \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall w \in a.\; (w \in k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in t) \wedge \\ \quad h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k) \wedge \\ \quad y \in k \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{encr}(h, y) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad h \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \end{array}}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} IS-HONEST(isp, c, I) (structure-library/strand-honesty.scm): every adversary entry point of the bundle into I lies on a TEXT trace -- the user's model merges the paper's M and K strands into one text trace of the known tokens ADV-TOKENS. 'S subset of T u K' is S a set of tokens (keys are tokens); 'K subset of S u k\textasciicircum{}-1' is: every key y is in S or KINV(y) is in KS. \renewcommand{\thethm}{6.12}
\begin{cor}[{A secret key reaching the network enters through a regular node}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-regular-entry}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-regular-entry}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, a, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)).\; ((y \in s) \vee (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(y) \in a)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; \neg (z \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \exists m \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}entry\text{-}point}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-token}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, x. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}token\text{-}set}(t) \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall w \in a.\; (w \in k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)) \wedge \\ \quad x \in t \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad x \in s \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{text-node-content}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad m \in \operatorname{nodes}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}text\text{-}trace}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p), \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(\operatorname{nth}(2, m))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p) \end{array}}

\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{6.13}
\begin{cor}[{Encryption under an uncompromised key does not originate with the adversary}]\label{thm:key-ideal-gen-no-adversary-origin}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-no-adversary-origin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, a, s.; \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c), g, y. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)).\; ((y \in s) \vee (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(y) \in a)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; \neg (z \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}entry\text{-}point}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, n) \wedge \\ \quad g \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad y \in s \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), \operatorname{encr}(g, y), n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{adversary-sent-shapes}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad m \in \operatorname{nodes}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sent}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}text\text{-}trace}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p), \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(\operatorname{nth}(2, m))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{lst}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((1 \leq i) \wedge (i \leq \operatorname{length}(l))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{nth}(i, l)) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists l \in \operatorname{tuples}(\operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)))), q \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad 1 \leq q \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad q \leq \operatorname{length}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{nth}(q, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{lst}(l)) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))), k \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = \operatorname{encr}(h, k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = h) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))), k \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) = h \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(k))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists x. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{same\text{-}strand\text{-}before}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x, m) \wedge (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), x) = \operatorname{encr}(h, k)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{7.2}
\begin{lem}[{Server, initiator and responder strands are pairwise disjoint}]\label{thm:or-init-resp-disjoint}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-init-resp-disjoint}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, n, m, k, c, d, f, q, r, h, g. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, s, a, b, n, m, k)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, s, c, d, f, q, r, h, g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-init-serv-disjoint}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, n, m, k, c, d, f, g, h, q. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, s, a, b, n, m, k)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, s, c, d, f, g, h, q) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-resp-serv-disjoint}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, n, m, k, h, g, c, d, f, q, r, t. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, s, a, b, n, m, k, h, g)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, s, c, d, f, q, r, t) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{7.4}
\begin{thm}[{Otway-Rees session key secrecy}]\label{thm:or-session-key-secrecy}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-session-key-secrecy}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, v, a, b, d, f, m, k.; \forall z \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad v \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(v), a, b, d, f, m, k) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), k) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), z) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))), \{\mathit{orv} \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) : \neg (\mathit{orv} \in \{w \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) : ((w = \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a)) \vee ((w = \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b)) \vee (w = k)))\})\}, \operatorname{singleton}(k))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-regular-entry}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, a, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)).\; ((y \in s) \vee (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(y) \in a)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; \neg (z \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \exists m \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{node\text{-}content}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), m) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}entry\text{-}point}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-encr-atoms}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, a, s, h, y. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}token\text{-}set}(t) \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \forall w \in a.\; (w \in k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in t) \wedge \\ \quad h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k) \wedge \\ \quad y \in k \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{encr}(h, y) \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (h \in \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, a, s)) \wedge (y \in a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-serv-key-originates}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, c, d, m, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, c, d, m, k) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), k, [2, s]) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} S = \{K\_AS, K\_BS, K\} and k = K minus S as separations of the keys; the conclusion is for I\_k[\{K\}], obtained from I\_k[S] by minimality (the paper's appeal to 6.3). The key-cover hypothesis of 6.12 holds because the three keys of S are symmetric. No regular node is an entry point for I\_k[S]: each positive regular content is shown outside the ideal component by component (6.8, an encryption's plaintext and key by key-ideal-gen-encr-atoms, a token of S only as the session key of a server strand, which by unique origination of K is s\_serv itself, whose keys are in S); the responder's H, H2 put the preceding node in the ideal. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-3).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{7.5}
\begin{prop}[{Encryption under an uncompromised long-term key originates on a regular node}]\label{thm:or-ltkey-no-adversary-origin}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-ltkey-no-adversary-origin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, x.; \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c), g \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(x) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(g, \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(x)), n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-ltkey-not-regular-origin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, x, n. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge ((x \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p)) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(x), n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-subterms}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall t, k, t_{0}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}token\text{-}set}(t) \wedge ((k \in \mathbf{Set}) \wedge (t_{0} \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(t, k, k, \operatorname{singleton}(t_{0})) = \{w \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(t, k) : \operatorname{is\text{-}subterm}(t, k, t_{0}, w)\} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{key-ideal-gen-no-adversary-origin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, a, s.; \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c), g, y. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}infiltrated\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a.\; (y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)).\; ((y \in s) \vee (\operatorname{kinv}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))(y) \in a)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; (z \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall z \in s.\; \neg (z \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(p, n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{is\text{-}entry\text{-}point}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), n, \operatorname{key\text{-}ideal\text{-}gen}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), a, s)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}adversary\text{-}node}(p, n) \wedge \\ \quad g \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(p)), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad y \in s \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(p), \operatorname{encr}(g, y), n) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{7.6}
\begin{prop}[{Shapes of encrypted terms originating on regular strands}]\label{thm:or-regular-encr-shapes}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, x, n, h. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n) \wedge \\ \quad h \in \operatorname{msg\text{-}set}(\operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))), \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(h, \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(x)), n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists a, b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}text}(p, a) \wedge ((b \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))) \wedge (h = \operatorname{lst}([a, b]))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists a, c, d. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}text}(p, a) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}text}(p, c) \wedge ((d \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p)) \wedge (h = \operatorname{lst}([a, c, x, d]))))) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists a, c, d. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}text}(p, a) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}text}(p, c) \wedge ((d \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p)) \wedge (h = \operatorname{lst}([a, c, d, x]))))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/otway-\allowbreak{}rees-\allowbreak{}laws.scm} --- 2820 recorded steps.}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Stated as one disjunction over the three shapes: H = LST([N, K]) (N a text, K a key), H = LST([N, M, X, C]) or H = LST([N, M, C, X]) (N, M texts, C a name). Proven by the general literal subterm inverter dks-sub-cases! on each positive regular content; an encryption inside the responder's H or H2 is received earlier and does not originate. Proven 2026-10-26 (SB-3).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{7.7}
\begin{cor}[{Where the server's and the participants' encryptions originate}]\label{thm:or-77-server}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-77-server}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, x, n, c, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad x \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad k \in \operatorname{keys}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([c, k]), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(x)), n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{nth}(1, n) = 2 \wedge \\ \quad \quad \exists a, b, d. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{nth}(2, n)), a, x, b, c, d, k) \vee \\ \quad \quad \exists f, b, d. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{nth}(2, n)), x, f, c, b, d, k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), k, [2, \operatorname{nth}(2, n)]) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-77-initiator}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, n, c, d, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (a = b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad d \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([c, d, a, b]), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a)), n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{nth}(1, n) = 1 \wedge \\ \quad \quad \exists f. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{nth}(2, n)), a, b, c, d, f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), c, [1, \operatorname{nth}(2, n)]) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-77-responder}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, n, c, d, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (a = b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), n) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad d \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([c, d, a, b]), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b)), n) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{nth}(1, n) = 2 \wedge \\ \quad \quad \exists f, g, h. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(\operatorname{nth}(2, n)), a, b, c, d, f, g, h) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), c, [2, \operatorname{nth}(2, n)]) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-init-nonce-originates}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, t, a, b, n, m, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad t \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(t), a, b, n, m, k) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), n, [1, t]) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-resp-nonce-originates}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, t, a, b, n, m, k, h, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sk\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad t \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(t), a, b, n, m, k, h, g) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), n, [2, t]) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\begin{thm}[{Otway-Rees: the initiator's guarantee}]\label{thm:or-initiator-guarantee}

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, s, a, b, d, m, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (a = b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), d) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, d, m, k) \wedge \\ \quad [2, s] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists f \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists r \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (r \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}ids}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad [2, r] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists g, h, n. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(r), a, b, f, m, g, h, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists v \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (v \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}ids}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad [2, v] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(v), a, b, d, f, m, k) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-initiator-nonce-source}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, c, m, k, h, g, d, f, u, v. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, c, m, k) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), d) \wedge \\ \quad f \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad v \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([c, f, u, v]), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a)), d) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (f = m) \wedge ((u = a) \wedge (v = b)) \end{array}}

\begin{thm}[{Otway-Rees: the responder's guarantee}]\label{thm:or-responder-guarantee}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-responder-guarantee}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, c, s, a, b, d, m, k, h, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bundle}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{bspace}(c) = \operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (a = b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), d) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(a) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \neg (\operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b) \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}tokens}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, d, m, k, h, g) \wedge \\ \quad [3, s] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists i \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (i \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}ids}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad [1, i] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists f, n. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}init}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(i), a, b, f, m, n) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \exists v \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (v \in \operatorname{adv\text{-}ids}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad [2, v] \in \operatorname{bnodes}(c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists f. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}serv}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(v), a, b, f, d, m, k) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{or-responder-nonce-source}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall p, s, a, b, c, m, k, h, g, d, f, u, v. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}space}(p) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{ids}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}or\text{-}resp}(p, \operatorname{strand\text{-}map}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)))(s), a, b, c, m, k, h, g) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{uniquely\text{-}originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regular\text{-}node}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p), d) \wedge \\ \quad f \in \operatorname{tokens}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p))) \wedge \\ \quad u \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad v \in \operatorname{sk\text{-}names}(p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{originates}(\operatorname{ispace}(\operatorname{sk\text{-}inf}(p)), \operatorname{encr}(\operatorname{lst}([c, f, u, v]), \operatorname{ltkey}(p)(b)), d) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (f = m) \wedge ((u = a) \wedge (v = b)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bundle-subterm-originates}}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.2}
\begin{prop}[{The atoms of a finite algebra of sets}]\label{thm:finite-algebra-atoms}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{finite-algebra-atoms}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, d. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}(c, d) \wedge (|d| \in \mathbb{N})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{atoms}(d) \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad \quad |\operatorname{atoms}(d)| \in \mathbb{N} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall a, b. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((a \in \operatorname{atoms}(d)) \wedge ((b \in \operatorname{atoms}(d)) \wedge \neg (a = b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (a \cap b) = \emptyset \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall a \in d. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((a = \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(u, \{s \in \operatorname{atoms}(d) : (s \subseteq a)\}, u)) \wedge (a = \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(u, \operatorname{atoms}(d), (a \cap u)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{algebra-point-atom}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b.; \forall x \in a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}(a, b) \wedge (|b| \in \mathbb{N})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \{y \in a : \forall \mathit{mmb} \in \{c \in b : (x \in c)\}.\; (y \in \mathit{mmb})\} \in \operatorname{atoms}(b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad x \in \{y \in a : \forall \mathit{mmb} \in \{c \in b : (x \in c)\}.\; (y \in \mathit{mmb})\} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{mqb} \in b. \\ \quad \quad \quad (x \in \mathit{mqb}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \{y \in a : \forall \mathit{mmb} \in \{c \in b : (x \in c)\}.\; (y \in \mathit{mmb})\} \subseteq \mathit{mqb} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{atoms-pairwise-disjoint}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, d, a, b. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}(c, d) \wedge ((a \in \operatorname{atoms}(d)) \wedge ((b \in \operatorname{atoms}(d)) \wedge \neg (a = b)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (a \cap b) = \emptyset \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{algebra-atom-decomposition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall b, c.; \forall a \in c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}(b, c) \wedge (|c| \in \mathbb{N})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad ((a = \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(u, \{s \in \operatorname{atoms}(c) : (s \subseteq a)\}, u)) \wedge (a = \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(u, \operatorname{atoms}(c), (a \cap u)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.4}
\begin{prop}[{Finite unions of a semi-algebra form an algebra}]\label{thm:finite-unions-algebra}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, i. \\ \quad a \in \mathbf{Set} \wedge \\ \quad i \subseteq \operatorname{power}(a) \wedge \\ \quad \exists e.\; (e \in i) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mia}, b.\; (((\mathit{mia} \in i) \wedge (b \in i)) \Rightarrow ((\mathit{mia} \cap b) \in i)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mia} \in i.\; (\operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(a, \mathit{mia}) \in \operatorname{finite\text{-}unions}(a, i)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}(a, \operatorname{finite\text{-}unions}(a, i)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/measure-\allowbreak{}ch1-\allowbreak{}algebras.scm} --- 46 recorded steps.}
%

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{arith}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} FINITE-UNIONS(omega, cI) defined (unions of finite subfamilies). The family is assumed non-empty, which the notes leave implicit (an empty family gives \{EMPTY-SET\}).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.6}
\begin{cor}[{Finite unions of rectangles in R\textasciicircum{}n form an algebra}]\label{thm:rn-rectangles-finite-unions-algebra}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{rn-rectangles-finite-unions-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}algebra\text{-}of\text{-}sets}((\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{R}), \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{finite\text{-}unions}((\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{R}), \operatorname{rn\text{-}rectangles}(n))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rn-rectangles-inter-closed}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, a, b. \\ \quad ((a \in \operatorname{rn\text{-}rectangles}(n)) \wedge (b \in \operatorname{rn\text{-}rectangles}(n))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (a \cap b) \in \operatorname{rn\text{-}rectangles}(n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rn-rectangle-complement-finite-union}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, j \in (\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R})). \\ \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n).\; \operatorname{is\text{-}interval}(j(i)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}((\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{R}), \operatorname{rn\text{-}box}(n, j)) \\ \quad \quad \in\; \operatorname{finite\text{-}unions}((\operatorname{interval}(1, n) \to \mathbb{R}), \operatorname{rn\text{-}rectangles}(n)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.14}
\begin{prop}[{The pullback sigma-algebra}]\label{thm:pullback-sigma-algebra}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-sigma-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, a_{2}, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a_{2}, b) \wedge (f \in (a \to a_{2}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f), a_{2}, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall c. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, c) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, c, a_{2}, b, f)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f) \subseteq c \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-sigma-is-sigma-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, a_{2}, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a_{2}, b) \wedge (f \in (a \to a_{2}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-sigma-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, a_{2}, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a_{2}, b) \wedge (f \in (a \to a_{2}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f), a_{2}, b, f) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-sigma-smallest}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, a_{2}, f, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a_{2}, b) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (a \to a_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, c, a_{2}, b, f) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f) \subseteq c \end{array}}

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.22}
\begin{prop}[{Pulling a measure back along a surjection}]\label{thm:pullback-measure-exists-unique}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-measure-exists-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, c, a_{2}, f, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, c, u) \wedge ((f \in (a \to a_{2})) \wedge \forall y \in a_{2}.\; \exists x \in a.\; (f(x) = y))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, c, f), \operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, c, f, u)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall b \in c.\; (\operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, c, f, u)(\{\mathit{mpx} \in a : (f(\mathit{mpx}) \in b)\}) = u(b)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall d. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, c, f), d) \wedge \forall b \in c.\; (d(\{\mathit{mpx} \in a : (f(\mathit{mpx}) \in b)\}) = u(b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad d = \operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, c, f, u) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-measure-is-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, a_{2}, f, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, b, u) \wedge ((f \in (a \to a_{2})) \wedge \forall y \in a_{2}.\; \exists x \in a.\; (f(x) = y))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, b, f), \operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, b, f, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-measure-value}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, c, a_{2}, f, u.; \forall b \in c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, c, u) \wedge ((f \in (a \to a_{2})) \wedge \forall y \in a_{2}.\; \exists x \in a.\; (f(x) = y))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, c, f, u)(\{\mathit{mpx} \in a : (f(\mathit{mpx}) \in b)\}) = u(b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pullback-measure-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, c, a_{2}, f, u, d. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, c, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (a \to a_{2}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall y \in a_{2}.\; \exists x \in a.\; (f(x) = y) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{pullback\text{-}sigma}(a, c, f), d) \wedge \\ \quad \forall b \in c.\; (d(\{\mathit{mpx} \in a : (f(\mathit{mpx}) \in b)\}) = u(b)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad d = \operatorname{pullback\text{-}measure}(a, c, f, u) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/measure-\allowbreak{}ch1-\allowbreak{}pullback.scm} --- 16 recorded steps.}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.23}
\begin{prop}[{No translation-invariant measure on all subsets of R (Vitali)}]\label{thm:vitali-no-invariant-measure}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{vitali-no-invariant-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\neg \exists u.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), u) \wedge (\forall s \in \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), t \in \mathbb{R}.\; (u((s + t)) = u(s)) \wedge ((0 < u(\operatorname{ccint}(0, 1))) \wedge (u(\operatorname{ccint}(0, 1)) \in \mathbb{R}))))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{vitali-null-case}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall s \in \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), t \in \mathbb{R}.\; (u((s + t)) = u(s)) \wedge \\ \quad 0 < u(\operatorname{ccint}(0, 1)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg (u(\{h \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1) : \exists x \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1).\; (h = \varepsilon(\{y \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1) : ((y - x) \in \{d \in \mathbb{R} : \exists a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}.\; ((a - b) = ((c + 1) \cdot d))\})\}))\}) = 0) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{vitali-positive-case}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall s \in \operatorname{power}(\mathbb{R}), t \in \mathbb{R}.\; (u((s + t)) = u(s)) \wedge \\ \quad u(\operatorname{ccint}(0, 1)) \in \mathbb{R} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg (0 < u(\{h \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1) : \exists x \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1).\; (h = \varepsilon(\{y \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1) : ((y - x) \in \{d \in \mathbb{R} : \exists a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}.\; ((a - b) = ((c + 1) \cdot d))\})\}))\})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.5}
\begin{prop}[{Measurable functions into a separable metric space are uniform limits of step functions}]\label{thm:step-map-approximation}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{step-map-approximation}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, s, f, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(s) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, \operatorname{pts}(s), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s), f) \wedge \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(c))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists g. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}step\text{-}map}(a, b, s, g) \wedge \forall x \in a.\; (\operatorname{dist}(s)(f(x), g(x)) < c) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{step-map-uniform-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, s, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, \operatorname{pts}(s), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s), f)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists c \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{pts}(s))). \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}step\text{-}map}(a, b, s, c(n)) \wedge \forall x \in a.\; (\operatorname{dist}(s)(f(x), c(n)(x)) < \operatorname{recip}((n + 1)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.7}
\begin{thm}[{Existence and uniqueness of the integral of non-negative functions}]\label{thm:integral-unique}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, j, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mdf}.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{mdf}) \Rightarrow (j(\mathit{mdf}) \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mda} \in b.\; (j(\operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{mda})) = u(\mathit{mda})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mda} \in b. \\ \quad \quad (u(\mathit{mda}) = 0) \Rightarrow (j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}scale}(a, \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}, \operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{mda}))) = 0) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mdf}, g. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{mdf}) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}eplus}(a, \mathit{mdf}, g)) = \operatorname{eplus}(j(\mathit{mdf}), j(g)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mdf}.; \forall c \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{mdf}) \wedge (0 \leq c)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}scale}(a, c, \mathit{mdf})) = \operatorname{etimes}(c, j(\mathit{mdf})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mdf}, g. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{mdf}) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, \mathit{mdf}, g))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\mathit{mdf}) \leq j(g) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mdcf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})). \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{mdcf}(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, \operatorname{mdcf}(n), \operatorname{mdcf}((n + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}sup}(a, \mathit{mdcf})) = \operatorname{esup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; j(\operatorname{mdcf}(n))), \mathbb{N})) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad j(f) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-unique-simple}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, j, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall f.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \Rightarrow (j(f) \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mda} \in b.\; (j(\operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{mda})) = u(\mathit{mda})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall f, g. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}eplus}(a, f, g)) = \operatorname{eplus}(j(f), j(g)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall f.; \forall c \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge (0 \leq c)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad j(\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}scale}(a, c, f)) = \operatorname{etimes}(c, j(f)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad j(s) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, s) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.9}
\begin{prop}[{Conull sets are closed under countable intersections and supersets}]\label{thm:conull-countable-inter}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{conull-countable-inter}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge ((f \in (\mathbb{N} \to b)) \wedge \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}conull}(a, b, u, f(k)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}conull}(a, b, u, \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(a, \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(a, f(n))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{conull-superset}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, \alpha, \beta. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}conull}(a, b, u, \alpha) \wedge ((\beta \in b) \wedge (\alpha \subseteq \beta)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}conull}(a, b, u, \beta) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{null-countable-union}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge ((f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(a))) \wedge \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, f(k)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, f(n))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.10}
\begin{prop}[{Functions equal almost everywhere have the same integral}]\label{thm:integral-ae-eq}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-ae-eq}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad c \in b \wedge \\ \quad u(c) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in c) \Rightarrow (f(x) = g(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-le-off-null}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, d, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad c \in b \wedge \\ \quad u(c) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in c) \Rightarrow (d(x) \leq f(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, d) \leq \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
