\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.15}
\begin{prop}[{The integral does not depend on the approximating sequence}]\label{thm:monotone-convergence}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{monotone-convergence}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, f(n), f((n + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}sup}(a, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}sup}(a, f)) = \operatorname{esup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f(n))), \mathbb{N})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-simple}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, s) = \operatorname{simple\text{-}integral}(a, u, s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-sup-of-simple}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{esup}(\{y \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star} : \exists s \in (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star}).\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, s) \wedge (\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, s, f) \wedge (y = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, s))))\}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.16}
\begin{prop}[{The monotone convergence theorem}]\label{thm:construction-of-measures-2.16}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, f(n), f((n + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}sup}(a, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}sup}(a, f)) = \operatorname{esup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f(n))), \mathbb{N})) \end{array}}

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.17}
\begin{prop}[{Hoelder's inequality}]\label{thm:hoelder}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hoelder}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, g.; \forall p, q \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad 1 < p \wedge \\ \quad 1 < q \wedge \\ \quad (/(1, p) + /(1, q)) = 1 \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}etimes}(a, f, g)) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(I_{p}({f}), I_{q}({g})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{young-extended}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star}, p, q \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((1 < p) \wedge ((1 < q) \wedge ((/(1, p) + /(1, q)) = 1))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{etimes}(a, b) \leq \operatorname{eplus}(\operatorname{etimes}(\operatorname{recip}(p), {a}^{p}), \operatorname{etimes}(\operatorname{recip}(q), {b}^{q})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\begin{lem}[{Young's inequality}]\label{thm:young-extended}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{young-extended}}

\vnbpart{\texttt{young-scaled}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c, d \in \mathbb{R}, u, v \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star}, p, q \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < c) \wedge ((0 < d) \wedge ((1 < p) \wedge ((1 < q) \wedge ((/(1, p) + /(1, q)) = 1))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{etimes}((c \cdot d), \operatorname{etimes}(u, v)) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{eplus}(\operatorname{etimes}((\operatorname{recip}(p) \cdot {c}^{p}), {u}^{p}), \operatorname{etimes}((\operatorname{recip}(q) \cdot {d}^{q}), {v}^{q})) \end{array}}

\end{lem}

\begin{prop}[{Minkowski's inequality}]\label{thm:minkowski}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, g.; \forall p \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge (1 \leq p)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad I_{p}({\operatorname{ptwise\text{-}eplus}(a, f, g)}) \leq \operatorname{eplus}(I_{p}({f}), I_{p}({g})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.21}
\begin{prop}[{Functions equal almost everywhere have the same integral}]\label{thm:construction-of-measures-2.21}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{integral-ae-eq}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad c \in b \wedge \\ \quad u(c) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in c) \Rightarrow (f(x) = g(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rintegral-ae-eq}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, g, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, s) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in s) \Rightarrow (f(x) = g(x))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, g) \wedge (\operatorname{rintegral}(a, b, u, g) = \operatorname{rintegral}(a, b, u, f)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.22}
\begin{thm}[{The L\textasciicircum{}p seminorm}]\label{thm:lp-norm-triangle}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{lp-norm-triangle}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, p, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad p \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 1 \leq p \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \|{(\lambda x \in a.\; (f(x) + g(x)))}\|_{p} \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{eplus}(\|{f}\|_{p}, \|{g}\|_{p}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{lp-norm-homogeneous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, p, f, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge ((c \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((p \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge (0 < p))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \|{(\lambda x \in a.\; (c \cdot f(x)))}\|_{p} = \operatorname{etimes}(\lvert c \rvert, \|{f}\|_{p}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{lp-norm-zero-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, p, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad p \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < p \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \|{(\lambda \mathit{sx} \in a.\; (f(\mathit{sx}) - g(\mathit{sx})))}\|_{p} = 0 \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists s. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, s) \wedge \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in s) \Rightarrow (f(x) = g(x))) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.23}
\begin{prop}[{A function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere}]\label{thm:integral-finite-ae-finite}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge (\operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f) < \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\{x \in a : (f(x) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf})\} \in b) \wedge (u(\{x \in a : (f(x) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf})\}) = 0) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.24}
\begin{prop}[{A function with nonnegative integral over every measurable set is nonnegative almost everywhere}]\label{thm:rintegral-nonneg-on-sets-null}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{rintegral-nonneg-on-sets-null}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, f) \wedge \\ \quad \forall c \in b. \\ \quad \quad 0 \leq \operatorname{rintegral}(a, b, u, (\lambda x \in a.\; (f(x) \cdot \operatorname{indicator}(a, c)(x)))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \{\mathit{nx} \in a : (f(\mathit{nx}) < 0)\}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rintegral-decomposition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, c, d. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (a \to \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, d) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (c(x) \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (d(x) \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (f(x) = (c(x) - d(x))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, c) \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, d) \in \mathbb{R} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, f) \wedge (\operatorname{rintegral}(a, b, u, f) = (\operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, c) - \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, d)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.26}
\begin{thm}[{Fatou's lemma}]\label{thm:fatou}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{fatou}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f(n)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}liminf}(a, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}liminf}(a, f)) \leq \operatorname{eliminf}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f(n)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{measurable-fn-liminf}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, b) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f(n)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}liminf}(a, f)) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.28}
\begin{prop}[{The dominated convergence theorem}]\label{thm:dominated-convergence}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{dominated-convergence}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad c \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, c(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}le}(a, c(n), g) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, g) \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; \operatorname{econverges\text{-}to}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; c(n)(x)), f(x)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{econverges\text{-}to}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, c(n))), \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fatou}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f(n)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}liminf}(a, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}liminf}(a, f)) \leq \operatorname{eliminf}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, f(n)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{dominated-convergence}}}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.29}
\begin{cor}[{Dominated convergence in L\textasciicircum{}p}]\label{thm:lp-dominated-convergence}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, p, s, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad p \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 1 \leq p \wedge \\ \quad s \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, s(k)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \|{g}\|_{p} \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \exists c. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, c) \wedge \forall x \in a.\; (\neg (x \in c) \Rightarrow (\lvert s(k)(x) \rvert \leq g(x)))) \wedge \\ \quad \exists c. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall x \in a. \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (x \in c) \Rightarrow \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, (\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; s(k)(x)), f(x)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \|{f}\|_{p} \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{econverges\text{-}to}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \|{(\lambda \mathit{sx} \in a.\; (s(k)(\mathit{sx}) - f(\mathit{sx})))}\|_{p}), 0) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/lp-\allowbreak{}convergence.scm} --- 2813 recorded steps.}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.30}
\begin{cor}[{Step functions are dense in L\textasciicircum{}p}]\label{thm:step-functions-dense-lp}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{step-functions-dense-lp}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, p, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad p \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 1 \leq p \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \|{f}\|_{p} \in \mathbb{R} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists s \in (\mathbb{N} \to (a \to \mathbb{R})). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}step\text{-}fn}(a, b, s(k)) \wedge (\|{s(k)}\|_{p} \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{econverges\text{-}to}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \|{(\lambda x \in a.\; (s(k)(x) - f(x)))}\|_{p}), 0) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{simple-difference-step-fn}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, v. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, v)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}step\text{-}fn}(a, b, (\lambda x \in a.\; (u(x) - v(x)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.31}
\begin{prop}[{L\textasciicircum{}infinity is the dual of L\textasciicircum{}1}]\label{thm:linf-is-l1-dual}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{linf-is-l1-dual}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, u)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge (\operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f) \in \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, f), \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall f, c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, f), c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall g \in \operatorname{l1\text{-}set}(a, b, u). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, (\lambda x \in a.\; (f(x) \cdot g(x)))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f) \leq c \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall f, c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, f, c) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{ldf}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{ldf}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, \mathit{ldf}) \leq c \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall g \in \operatorname{l1\text{-}set}(a, b, u).\; (f(g) = \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, \mathit{ldf})(g)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{l1-pairing-bounded}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge (\operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f) \in \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, f), \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{l1-pairing-norm-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, f), c) \wedge \\ \quad \forall g \in \operatorname{l1\text{-}set}(a, b, u). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, (\lambda x \in a.\; (f(x) \cdot g(x)))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, f) \leq c \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{l1-dual-onto}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, f, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}bounded\text{-}l1\text{-}functional}(a, b, u, f, c))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{ldf}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, \mathit{ldf}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, \mathit{ldf}) \leq c \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall g \in \operatorname{l1\text{-}set}(a, b, u).\; (f(g) = \operatorname{l1\text{-}pairing}(a, b, u, \mathit{ldf})(g)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.32}
\begin{prop}[{Abstract change of variables}]\label{thm:pfw-change-of-variables}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pfw-change-of-variables}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, h, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, h) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, f))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(h(z)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a_{2}, c, \operatorname{push\text{-}forward}(a, c, u, h), f) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(h(z)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pfw-change-of-variables-real}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, h, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, h) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a_{2}, c, \operatorname{push\text{-}forward}(a, c, u, h), f) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(h(z)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{rintegral}(a_{2}, c, \operatorname{push\text{-}forward}(a, c, u, h), f) = \operatorname{rintegral}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(h(z)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pfw-integrable-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, h, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, h) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, f))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a_{2}, c, \operatorname{push\text{-}forward}(a, c, u, h), f) \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \operatorname{is\text{-}integrable}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(h(z)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pfw-simple-change-of-variables}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, h, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, h) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}simple\text{-}fn}(a, b, (\lambda z \in a.\; s(h(z)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(a_{2}, c, \operatorname{push\text{-}forward}(a, c, u, h), s) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; s(h(z)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.35}
\begin{cor}[{A measure isomorphism induces isomorphisms of L\textasciicircum{}p}]\label{thm:measure-isomorphism-lp-isomorphism}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{measure-isomorphism-lp-isomorphism}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, d, h, t. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, d, h) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}measure\text{-}isomorphism}(a, b, u, a_{2}, d, h, t))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, d, f) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall p \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (1 \leq p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \|{(\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))}\|_{p} = \|{f}\|_{p} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))) = \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a_{2}, d, h, f) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall f, g \in (a_{2} \to \mathbb{R}), c \in \mathbb{R}, x \in a. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda z \in a.\; (\lambda y \in a_{2}.\; (f(y) + (c \cdot g(y))))(t(z)))(x) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))(x) + (c \cdot (\lambda z \in a.\; g(t(z)))(x)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall g. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists f. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, d, f) \wedge \forall x \in a.\; (g(x) = f(t(x))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{comp-measure-preserving-lp-norm}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, d, t, f, p. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, t) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mib} \in c.\; (d(\mathit{mib}) = u(\{x \in a : (t(x) \in \mathit{mib})\})) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, f) \wedge \\ \quad p \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < p \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \|{(\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))}\|_{p} = \|{f}\|_{p} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{comp-measure-preserving-linf-norm}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, a_{2}, c, d, t, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a_{2}, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}map}(a, b, a_{2}, c, t) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mib} \in c.\; (d(\mathit{mib}) = u(\{x \in a : (t(x) \in \mathit{mib})\})) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}real\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a_{2}, c, f) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a, b, u, (\lambda z \in a.\; f(t(z)))) = \operatorname{linf\text{-}norm}(a_{2}, c, d, f) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.2}
\begin{prop}[{Characterisation of complete measures}]\label{thm:complete-iff-symdiff}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{complete-iff-symdiff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \forall \alpha, \beta. \\ \quad \quad \quad \alpha \subseteq a \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \beta \subseteq a \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \operatorname{sym\text{-}difference}(\alpha, \beta)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \alpha \in b \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \beta \in b \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{null-set-subset}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, \mathit{nsa}, \mathit{nsb}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \mathit{nsa}) \wedge (\mathit{nsb} \subseteq \mathit{nsa})) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \mathit{nsb}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.3}
\begin{prop}[{The completion of a measure}]\label{thm:completion-sigma-algebra}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-sigma-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, b, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-measure-is-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, b, u), \operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, b, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-measure-extends}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (c \in b)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, b, u)(c) = u(c)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-measure-value}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge ((c \in b) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, b, u)((c \cup s)) = u(c) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-measure-complete}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, b, u), \operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, b, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-measure-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c.; \forall x \in \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, b, u). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, b, u), c) \wedge \\ \quad \forall d \in b.\; (c(d) = u(d)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad c(x) = \operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, b, u)(x) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.4}
\begin{prop}[{A complete measure extends the completion of its restriction}]\label{thm:complete-extends-completion}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{complete-extends-completion}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c.; \forall x \in \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, c, \operatorname{res}(u, c)). \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, c) \wedge (c \subseteq b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad u(x) = \operatorname{completion\text{-}measure}(a, c, \operatorname{res}(u, c))(x) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{completion-of-restrict-in}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, c) \wedge (c \subseteq b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{completion\text{-}sigma}(a, c, \operatorname{res}(u, c)) \subseteq b \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{measure-restrict}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, c) \wedge (c \subseteq b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, c, \operatorname{res}(u, c)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.5}
\begin{prop}[{Sections of a product-measurable function are measurable}]\label{thm:x-section-measurable}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{x-section-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, b, c, d, x. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(s, a) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(b, c) \wedge ((d \in \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c)) \wedge (x \in s)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{x\text{-}section}(b, d, x) \in c \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fn-x-section-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, b, c, f, x. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(s, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}((s \times b), \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c), f) \wedge \\ \quad x \in s \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(b, c, \operatorname{fn\text{-}x\text{-}section}(b, f, x)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fn-y-section-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, b, c, f, y. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(s, a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}((s \times b), \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c), f) \wedge \\ \quad y \in b \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(s, a, \operatorname{fn\text{-}y\text{-}section}(s, f, y)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.7}
\begin{thm}[{Fubini}]\label{thm:fubini}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{fubini}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, u, b, c, d, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}((s \times b), \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c), f) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(s, a, \operatorname{x\text{-}section\text{-}integral}(s, b, c, d, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(b, c, \operatorname{y\text{-}section\text{-}integral}(s, a, u, b, f)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{integral}(s, a, u, \operatorname{x\text{-}section\text{-}integral}(s, b, c, d, f)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{integral}(b, c, d, \operatorname{y\text{-}section\text{-}integral}(s, a, u, b, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{fubini-sets}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, u, b, c, d, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad f \in \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}fubini\text{-}set}(s, a, u, b, c, d, f) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{dynkin-pi-lambda}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, d, p. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}dynkin\text{-}system}(a, d) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}pi\text{-}system}(p) \wedge (p \subseteq d))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{sigma\text{-}generated}(a, p) \subseteq d \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.8}
\begin{defn}[{The product measure}]\label{thm:product-measure-is-measure}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{product-measure-is-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, u, b, c, d. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(b, c, d) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}((s \times b), \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c), \operatorname{product\text{-}measure}(s, a, u, b, c, d)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{product-measure-symmetric}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, u, b, c, d, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(s, a, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(b, c, d) \wedge \\ \quad f \in \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(s, a, b, c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{product\text{-}measure}(s, a, u, b, c, d)(f) = \operatorname{integral}(b, c, d, \operatorname{y\text{-}section\text{-}measure}(s, b, u, f)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{product-measure-rectangle}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, u, b, c, d, f, g. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(s, a, u) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, d) \wedge ((f \in a) \wedge (g \in c)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{product\text{-}measure}(s, a, u, b, c, d)((f \times g)) = \operatorname{etimes}(u(f), d(g)) \end{array}}
%
\end{defn}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.10}
\begin{thm}[{Radon-Nikodym theorem}]\label{thm:radon-nikodym}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{radon-nikodym}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}absolutely\text{-}continuous}(a, b, u, c) \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists q. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, q) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{rna} \in b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad u(\mathit{rna}) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, c, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}etimes}(a, q, \operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{rna}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{radon-nikodym-sigma-finite}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}finite}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}absolutely\text{-}continuous}(a, b, u, c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists q. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, q) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{rna} \in b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad u(\mathit{rna}) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, c, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}etimes}(a, q, \operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{rna}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{radon-nikodym-finite}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad u(a) \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad c(a) \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}absolutely\text{-}continuous}(a, b, u, c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists q. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, q) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{rna} \in b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad u(\mathit{rna}) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, c, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}etimes}(a, q, \operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{rna}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{density-implies-absolutely-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{rna} \in b. \\ \quad \quad u(\mathit{rna}) = \operatorname{integral}(a, b, c, \operatorname{ptwise\text{-}etimes}(a, f, \operatorname{indicator}(a, \mathit{rna}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}absolutely\text{-}continuous}(a, b, u, c) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.12}
\begin{prop}[{Jordan decomposition of a signed measure}]\label{thm:jordan-decomposition}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{jordan-decomposition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall b, c, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}signed\text{-}measure}(b, c, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, \operatorname{pos\text{-}variation}(c, u)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, \operatorname{neg\text{-}variation}(c, u)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall \alpha \in c.\; (\operatorname{pos\text{-}variation}(c, u)(\alpha) \in \mathbb{R}) \vee \\ \quad \quad \forall \alpha \in c.\; (\operatorname{neg\text{-}variation}(c, u)(\alpha) \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall a \in c. \\ \quad \quad \quad u(a) = \operatorname{ext\text{-}sub}(\operatorname{pos\text{-}variation}(c, u)(a), \operatorname{neg\text{-}variation}(c, u)(a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pos-variation-is-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}signed\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, \operatorname{pos\text{-}variation}(b, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{neg-variation-is-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}signed\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, \operatorname{neg\text{-}variation}(b, u)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{jordan-decomposition}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/jordan-\allowbreak{}decomposition.scm} --- 19 recorded steps.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{pos-variation-is-measure}, \texttt{neg-variation-is-measure}, \texttt{signed-measure-one-variation-finite}, \texttt{jordan-decomposition-value}.}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.17}
\begin{prop}[{Polar decomposition of a complex measure}]\label{thm:polar-decomposition-exists}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{polar-decomposition-exists}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complex\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists v. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}finite\text{-}measure}(a, b, v) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \alpha \in b.\; ((v(\alpha) = 0) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}complex\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, u, \alpha)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complex\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\operatorname{magnitude}(c(x)) = 1) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \alpha \in b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad u(\alpha) = \operatorname{complex\text{-}integral}(a, b, v, (\lambda \mathit{cux} \in a.\; (\operatorname{indicator}(a, \alpha)(\mathit{cux}) \cdot c(\mathit{cux})))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{polar-decomposition-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u, c, d, f, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}finite\text{-}measure}(a, b, c) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}finite\text{-}measure}(a, b, d) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complex\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, f) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complex\text{-}measurable\text{-}fn}(a, b, g) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\operatorname{magnitude}(f(x)) = 1) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in a.\; (\operatorname{magnitude}(g(x)) = 1) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \alpha \in b. \\ \quad \quad u(\alpha) = \operatorname{complex\text{-}integral}(a, b, c, (\lambda \mathit{cux} \in a.\; (\operatorname{indicator}(a, \alpha)(\mathit{cux}) \cdot f(\mathit{cux})))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \alpha \in b. \\ \quad \quad u(\alpha) = \operatorname{complex\text{-}integral}(a, b, d, (\lambda \mathit{cux} \in a.\; (\operatorname{indicator}(a, \alpha)(\mathit{cux}) \cdot g(\mathit{cux})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\forall \alpha \in b.\; (c(\alpha) = d(\alpha)) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, c, \{\mathit{ux} \in a : \neg (f(\mathit{ux}) = g(\mathit{ux}))\})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.2 (corollary)}
\begin{cor}[{A translation-invariant Borel measure on the line is a multiple of Lebesgue measure}]\label{thm:lebesgue-translation-invariant}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{lebesgue-translation-invariant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, k, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}), u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall v, c. \\ \quad \quad ((v \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms})) \wedge ((c \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((v + c) \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms})))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad u((v + c)) = u(v) \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < k \wedge \\ \quad u(\operatorname{ccint}(0, 1)) = k \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u(s) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{etimes}(k, \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{res}(\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{closed\text{-}intervals}, (\lambda \mathit{ols} \in \operatorname{closed\text{-}intervals}.\; \operatorname{interval\text{-}length}(\mathit{ols}))), \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{closed\text{-}intervals}, (\lambda \mathit{ols} \in \operatorname{closed\text{-}intervals}.\; \operatorname{interval\text{-}length}(\mathit{ols})))))(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{esum-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c \in \mathbb{R}, d.; \forall f \in (d \to \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star}). \\ \quad (0 \leq c) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{esum}((\lambda z \in d.\; \operatorname{etimes}(c, f(z)))) = \operatorname{etimes}(c, \operatorname{esum}(f))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{measure-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, u.; \forall c \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge (0 \leq c)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, (\lambda x \in b.\; \operatorname{etimes}(c, u(x)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.4}
\begin{prop}[{The Caratheodory theorem}]\label{thm:caratheodory-measurable-sigma-algebra}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-measurable-sigma-algebra}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}algebra}(a, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u), \operatorname{res}(u, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-null-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \wedge ((s \subseteq a) \wedge (u(s) = 0))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}caratheodory\text{-}measurable}(a, u, s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-superadditive-suffices}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \wedge \\ \quad s \subseteq a \wedge \\ \quad \forall \alpha \in \operatorname{power}(a). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{eplus}(u((\alpha \cap s)), u(\operatorname{difference}(\alpha, s))) \leq u(\alpha) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}caratheodory\text{-}measurable}(a, u, s) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.5}
\begin{lem}[{Outer measure is additive on disjoint measurable pieces}]\label{thm:outer-measure-disjoint-additive}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{outer-measure-disjoint-additive}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u, f, \mathit{ta}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \wedge \\ \quad f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall i, j. \\ \quad \quad ((i \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge ((j \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge \neg (i = j))) \Rightarrow ((f(i) \cap f(j)) = \emptyset) \wedge \\ \quad \mathit{ta} \in \operatorname{power}(a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u((\mathit{ta} \cap \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, f(n)))) = \operatorname{esum}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; u((\mathit{ta} \cap f(n))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-prefix-split}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, a, u, f, \alpha. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \wedge ((f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u))) \wedge (\alpha \in \operatorname{power}(a)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad u(\alpha) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{eplus}(\operatorname{finsum}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star\text{-}add\text{-}monoid}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; u((\alpha \cap \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(f(k), \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(j, \mathrm{OS}(k), f(j)))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathrm{OS}(n)), \\ \quad \quad \quad u(\operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(\alpha, \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(j, \mathrm{OS}(n), f(j))))) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%

%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.10}
\begin{prop}[{The outer measure extending a measure}]\label{thm:method-i-outer-extends}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-extends}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge (c \in b)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)(c) = o(c)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-measurable}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, c. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge (c \in b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}caratheodory\text{-}measurable}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o), c) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-null-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge (s \in \operatorname{power}(a))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)(s) = 0) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, o, s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-finite-approx}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}caratheodory\text{-}measurable}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o), s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)(s) \in \mathbb{R} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists y \in b.\; ((s \subseteq y) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, o, \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(y, s))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-of-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge (s \in \operatorname{power}(a))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)(s) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{einf}(\{v \in \operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star} : \exists \mathit{osa} \in b.\; ((s \subseteq \mathit{osa}) \wedge (v = o(\mathit{osa})))\}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.11}
\begin{cor}[{The Caratheodory measure of mu* is complete and extends the completion of rho}]\label{thm:method-i-outer-caratheodory-complete}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-caratheodory-complete}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)), \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{res}(\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o), \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-i-outer-extends-completion}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, o, c, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, o) \wedge ((c \in b) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}null\text{-}set}(a, b, o, s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (c \cup s) \in \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{res}(\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o), \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, b, o)))((c \cup s)) = o(c) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{caratheodory-measure-complete}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, u. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(a, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete\text{-}measure}(a, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u), \operatorname{res}(u, \operatorname{caratheodory\text{-}sets}(a, u))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.17}
\begin{prop}[{Extensions of a local measure agree on B-sigma}]\label{thm:local-measure-extensions-agree}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, o, u, d, g. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}measure}(a, b, c, o) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, d) \wedge \\ \quad \forall e \in c.\; (u(e) = o(e)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall e \in c.\; (d(e) = o(e)) \wedge \\ \quad g \in (\mathbb{N} \to c) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u(\operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, g(n))) = d(\operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, g(n))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.18}
\begin{prop}[{The method-I extension is the largest}]\label{thm:local-measure-extension-le-outer}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{local-measure-extension-le-outer}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, o, u, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}measure}(a, b, c, o) \wedge \\ \quad \emptyset \in c \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, u) \wedge \\ \quad \forall e \in c.\; (u(e) = o(e)) \wedge \\ \quad s \in b \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u(s) \leq \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, c, o)(s) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{local-measure-max-extension}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c, o. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}measure}(a, b, c, o) \wedge (\emptyset \in c)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(a, b, \operatorname{restrict}(\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, c, o), b)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall e \in c.\; (\operatorname{restrict}(\operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(a, c, o), b)(e) = o(e)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.22}
\begin{prop}[{The minimum extension of a local measure}]\label{thm:local-measure-min-extension}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall b, c, d, o. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}measure}(b, c, d, o) \wedge (\emptyset \in d)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists m. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall e \in d.\; (m(e) = o(e)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall u.; \forall s \in c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}measure}(b, c, u) \wedge \forall e \in d.\; (u(e) = o(e))) \Rightarrow (m(s) \leq u(s)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall s \in c, a. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}union\text{-}of}(d, a) \wedge ((a \subseteq s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}locally\text{-}null}(c, d, o, \operatorname{difference}(s, a)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad m(s) = \operatorname{method\text{-}i\text{-}outer}(b, d, o)(a) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall s \in c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg \exists \mathit{mma} \in c.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}sigma\text{-}union\text{-}of}(d, \mathit{mma}) \wedge ((\mathit{mma} \subseteq s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}locally\text{-}null}(c, d, o, \operatorname{difference}(s, \mathit{mma})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad m(s) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf} \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.23}
\begin{prop}[{The method-II outer measure is a metric outer measure}]\label{thm:method-ii-metric-outer-measure}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-metric-outer-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), s, a)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(m, \operatorname{method\text{-}ii}(m, s, a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-outer-measure}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), s, a) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), \operatorname{method\text{-}ii}(m, s, a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-delta-outer}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a, l. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), s, a) \wedge ((l \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge (0 \leq l))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, s, a, l)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-delta-separated}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a, l, r, b, c. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), s, a) \wedge \\ \quad l \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 \leq l \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(r) \wedge \\ \quad l < r \wedge \\ \quad b \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in b, y \in c.\; (r \leq \operatorname{dist}(m)(x, y)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{eplus}(\operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, s, a, l)(b), \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, s, a, l)(c)) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, s, a, l)((b \cup c)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.27}
\begin{lem}[{A metric outer measure is additive on a positively separated sequence}]\label{thm:metric-outer-measure-separated-sum}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{metric-outer-measure-separated-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, u, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(m, u) \wedge \\ \quad s \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall k, l \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\neg (k = l) \Rightarrow \neg (\operatorname{set\text{-}dist}(m, s(k), s(l)) = 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u(\operatorname{big\text{-}union}(n, \mathbb{N}, s(n))) = \operatorname{esum}((\lambda n \in \mathbb{N}.\; u(s(n)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{metric-outer-measure-finite-separated}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, u, s.; \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(m, u) \wedge \\ \quad s \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall k, l \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\neg (k = l) \Rightarrow \neg (\operatorname{set\text{-}dist}(m, s(k), s(l)) = 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad u(\operatorname{big\text{-}union}(j, \mathrm{OS}(n), s(j))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{finsum}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}pos\text{-}star\text{-}add\text{-}monoid}, (\lambda a \in \mathbb{N}.\; u(s(a))), \mathrm{OS}(n)) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.28}
\begin{lem}[{The layers of the complement of a closed set}]\label{thm:metric-outer-layers-limit}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, u, l. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}outer\text{-}measure}(m, u) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(m, l)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \{x \in \operatorname{pts}(m) : (\operatorname{recip}((n + 1)) \leq \operatorname{pt\text{-}set\text{-}dist}(m, x, l))\} \\ \quad \quad \quad \subseteq\; \{x \in \operatorname{pts}(m) : (\operatorname{recip}(((n + 1) + 1)) \leq \operatorname{pt\text{-}set\text{-}dist}(m, x, l))\} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall a \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)). \\ \quad \quad \quad u((a \cap \operatorname{complement\text{-}in}(\operatorname{pts}(m), l))) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{esup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; u((a \cap \{x \in \operatorname{pts}(m) : (\operatorname{recip}((k + 1)) \leq \operatorname{pt\text{-}set\text{-}dist}(m, x, l))\}))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathbb{N})) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Proof.} \texttt{theorem-\allowbreak{}library/metric-\allowbreak{}outer-\allowbreak{}measure.scm} --- 1092 recorded steps.}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.32}
\begin{prop}[{Comparison of Hausdorff measures for comparable metrics}]\label{thm:hausdorff-compare}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-compare}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, a, c, b, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pts}(a) = \operatorname{pts}(m) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < c \wedge \\ \quad \forall x, y \in \operatorname{pts}(m).\; (\operatorname{dist}(m)(x, y) \leq (c \cdot \operatorname{dist}(a)(x, y))) \wedge \\ \quad b \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < b \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{hausdorff}(m, b)(s) \leq \operatorname{etimes}({c}^{b}, \operatorname{hausdorff}(a, b)(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-compare}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, b, p, d, c, k, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pts}(b) = \operatorname{pts}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(m), \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), p) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}premeasure}(\operatorname{pts}(b), \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(b)), d) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < c \wedge \\ \quad k \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < k \wedge \\ \quad \forall a \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)).\; (\operatorname{diam}(m, a) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(c, \operatorname{diam}(b, a))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall a \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)).\; (p(a) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(k, d(a))) \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{method\text{-}ii}(m, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), p)(s) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(k, \operatorname{method\text{-}ii}(b, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(b)), d)(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diam-compare}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, b, c, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(b) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pts}(b) = \operatorname{pts}(m) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < c \wedge \\ \quad \forall x, y \in \operatorname{pts}(m).\; (\operatorname{dist}(m)(x, y) \leq (c \cdot \operatorname{dist}(b)(x, y))) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{diam}(m, a) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(c, \operatorname{diam}(b, a)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.38}
\begin{prop}[{Comparison of Hausdorff measures for a doubling function}]\label{thm:hausdorff-phi-compare}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-phi-compare}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, a, c, i. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pts}(a) = \operatorname{pts}(m) \wedge \\ \quad c \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < c \wedge \\ \quad \forall x, y \in \operatorname{pts}(m).\; (\operatorname{dist}(m)(x, y) \leq (c \cdot \operatorname{dist}(a)(x, y))) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(k) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall s \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}phi}(m, i)(s) \leq \operatorname{etimes}(k, \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}phi}(a, i)(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{doubling-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall i.; \forall c \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \wedge (0 < c)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(k) \wedge \forall r \in \mathbb{R}.\; ((0 \leq r) \Rightarrow (i((c \cdot r)) \leq (k \cdot i(r)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{doubling-power}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, i, l.; \forall r \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad i \in (\mathit{nnreal} \to \mathit{nnreal}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(l) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{mhr} \in \mathbb{R}.\; ((0 < \mathit{mhr}) \Rightarrow (i((2 \cdot \mathit{mhr})) \leq (l \cdot i(\mathit{mhr})))) \wedge \\ \quad 0 < r \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad i((\operatorname{power}(2, n) \cdot r)) \leq (\operatorname{power}(l, n) \cdot i(r)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.44}
\begin{prop}[{Doubling is invariant under bounded equivalence}]\label{thm:doubling-iff-boundedly-equivalent}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall i, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}boundedly\text{-}equivalent}(i, a) \wedge \\ \quad i(0) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad a(0) = 0 \wedge \\ \quad \forall r, q \in \mathit{nnreal}.\; ((r \leq q) \Rightarrow (i(r) \leq i(q))) \wedge \\ \quad \forall r, q \in \mathit{nnreal}.\; ((r \leq q) \Rightarrow (a(r) \leq a(q))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(a) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.53}
\begin{prop}[{Uniqueness of the Hausdorff dimension}]\label{thm:hausdorff-positive-infinite}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-positive-infinite}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, a, o, s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad a \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad o \in \mathbb{R} \wedge \\ \quad 0 < o \wedge \\ \quad o < a \wedge \\ \quad s \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad 0 < \operatorname{hausdorff}(m, a)(s) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{hausdorff}(m, o)(s) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-dim-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a, b. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}hausdorff\text{-}dim}(m, s, a) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}hausdorff\text{-}dim}(m, s, b)) \Rightarrow (a = b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-delta-below}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, d, o, a, s. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge (\operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(d) \wedge ((o \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((0 < o) \wedge ((a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((o < a) \wedge (s \in \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m))))))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{etimes}({d}^{(o - a)}, \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}pm}(m, a), d)(s)) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}pm}(m, o), d)(s) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.54}
\begin{prop}[{Local Hausdorff dimension in a separable space}]\label{thm:hausdorff-dim-local}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, r, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(m) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(r) \wedge \\ \quad \exists \mathit{mhx}.\; (\mathit{mhx} \in \operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{pts}(m).\; \operatorname{is\text{-}hausdorff\text{-}dim}(m, \operatorname{ball}(m, x, r), a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}hausdorff\text{-}dim}(m, \operatorname{pts}(m), a) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.55}
\begin{prop}[{Hausdorff measure restricts to Borel subsets}]\label{thm:hausdorff-phi-subspace}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{hausdorff-phi-subspace}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, i, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \wedge ((s \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge (a \subseteq s)))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}phi}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), i)(a) = \operatorname{hausdorff\text{-}phi}(m, i)(a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-delta-subspace-le}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, i, d, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \wedge ((s \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge ((d \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((0 \leq d) \wedge (a \subseteq s)))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), \operatorname{phi\text{-}pm}(m, i), d)(a) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s))), \operatorname{phi\text{-}pm}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), i), d)(a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{method-ii-delta-subspace-ge}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, i, d, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}doubling}(i) \wedge ((s \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge ((d \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((0 \leq d) \wedge (a \subseteq s)))))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s))), \operatorname{phi\text{-}pm}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), i), d)(a) \\ \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{method\text{-}ii\text{-}delta}(m, \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(m)), \operatorname{phi\text{-}pm}(m, i), d)(a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{subspace-diam}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, s, a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge ((s \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(m)) \wedge (a \subseteq s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(m, s), a) = \operatorname{diam}(m, a) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.2}
\begin{prop}[{Borel sets of a subspace are traces}]\label{thm:borel-sets-subspace}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{borel-sets-subspace}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, y, b. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (y \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (b \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, y))) \Leftrightarrow \exists e \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s).\; (b = (e \cap y)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mbs-trace-borel}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, y.; \forall e \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s). \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (y \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (e \cap y) \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, y)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mbs-borel-is-trace}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, y.; \forall b \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, y)). \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (y \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists e \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s).\; (b = (e \cap y)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.3}
\begin{prop}[{Borel sets of a product of separable spaces}]\label{thm:borel-sets-product}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{borel-sets-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(t)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{product2\text{-}ms}(s, t)) = \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(\operatorname{pts}(s), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s), \operatorname{pts}(t), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(t)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mbp-open-in-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, u. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(s) \wedge (\operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(t) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(\operatorname{product2\text{-}ms}(s, t), u))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad u \in \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(\operatorname{pts}(s), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s), \operatorname{pts}(t), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(t)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mbp-product-in-borel}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t.; \forall e \in \operatorname{product\text{-}sigma}(\operatorname{pts}(s), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(s), \operatorname{pts}(t), \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(t)). \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(t)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad e \in \operatorname{borel\text{-}sets}(\operatorname{product2\text{-}ms}(s, t)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.6}
\begin{prop}[{Sieve intersections are singletons}]\label{thm:nested-closed-intersection}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{nested-closed-intersection}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s.; \forall a \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(s))). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \exists x.\; (x \in a(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; (a((n + 1)) \subseteq a(n)) \wedge \\ \quad \forall b. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{mcbn} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; ((\mathit{mcbn} \leq n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{diam}(s, a(n)) \leq b)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists p \in \operatorname{pts}(s). \\ \quad \quad \quad (\forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p \in a(n)) \wedge \forall q \in \operatorname{pts}(s).\; (\forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; (q \in a(n)) \Rightarrow (q = p))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diam-dist-le}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, a.; \forall x, y \in a. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m) \wedge (a \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(m))) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{dist}(m)(x, y) \leq \operatorname{diam}(m, a)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proofs: the file that holds each, the lemmas it cites, its oracles and its bill.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{nested-closed-intersection}}}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.10}
\begin{prop}[{Souslin sets are continuous images of Baire space}]\label{thm:souslin-iff-baire-image}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{souslin-iff-baire-image}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, e. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e) \Leftrightarrow \exists f.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}baire\text{-}continuous}(s, f) \wedge (\operatorname{image}(f, (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N})) = e)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{baire-image-souslin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, f. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}baire\text{-}continuous}(s, f)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, \operatorname{image}(f, (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{souslin-baire-image}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, e. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists f.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}baire\text{-}continuous}(s, f) \wedge (\operatorname{image}(f, (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N})) = e)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\vnbpart{\texttt{complete-separable-souslin}}
\vnbstmt{\forall s.\; ((\operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(s)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, \operatorname{pts}(s)))}

\end{lem}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.14}
\begin{prop}[{Souslin sets are continuous images of Polish spaces}]\label{thm:souslin-iff-polish-image}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{souslin-iff-polish-image}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, e. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge (e \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e) \\ \quad \quad \Leftrightarrow\; \exists t. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists h.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(t, \operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, e), h) \wedge (\operatorname{image}(h, \operatorname{pts}(t)) = e)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{souslin-polish-image}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, e. \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists t. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists h.\; (\operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(t, \operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, e), h) \wedge (\operatorname{image}(h, \operatorname{pts}(t)) = e)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-image-polish-souslin}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, e, t, h. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \\ \quad e \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}separable}(t) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(t, \operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, e), h) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{image}(h, \operatorname{pts}(t)) = e \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{baire-ms-polish}}
\vnbstmt{\operatorname{is\text{-}polish}(\operatorname{baire\text{-}ms})}
%
\end{prop}

\begin{prop}[{Souslin sets closed under countable unions and intersections}]\label{thm:souslin-countable-union}

\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s.; \forall e \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(s))). \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e(k))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, \operatorname{big\text{-}union}(\mathit{mxk}, \mathbb{N}, e(\mathit{mxk}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{souslin-countable-intersection}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s.; \forall e \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{power}(\operatorname{pts}(s))). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, e(k)) \wedge \\ \quad \exists x.\; (x \in \{p \in \operatorname{pts}(s) : \forall \mathit{mxk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p \in e(\mathit{mxk}))\}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}souslin}(s, \{p \in \operatorname{pts}(s) : \forall \mathit{mxk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (p \in e(\mathit{mxk}))\}) \end{array}}

\end{prop}
